senses.title: The great disaster
senses.definition: a sudden violent event that changes the earth or a society
senses.definitionCN: 突然而猛烈、改变地貌或社会的事件
senses.example: The eruption was a cataclysm for the island.

senses.why: Greek kataklysmos meant a flood washing everything away.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 kataklysmos 指冲走一切的洪水。

senses.title: A violent change
senses.definition: a sudden great change in politics or society
senses.definitionCN: 政治或社会中的突然巨变
senses.example: The revolution was a cataclysm for the old order.
senses.exampleCN: 这场革命对旧秩序是场剧变。
senses.why: The flood image widened to any sweeping change.
senses.whyCN: 洪水意象扩展到任何席卷性的变化。

definition_zh: 削弱；减轻；使变细；使稀薄
definition_en: to make something weaker, thinner or less intense
core_image: 一根绳子被越拉越长，绳身越来越细，最后只剩一根发亮的丝
scene: 工程师把信号在长电缆里逐段变弱的过程画成一条向下弯的曲线。 Repeaters are placed along the cable so that the signal does not attenuate too quickly.
sceneCN: 这里 attenuate 指信号强度沿线路逐渐减弱（第 1 个义项：强度减弱）；句意为电缆沿线设置中继器，以免信号衰减过快。

senses.title: Reduce intensity
senses.definition: to make a force, effect or feeling weaker
senses.definitionCN: 使力量、效果或感受变弱
senses.example: Thick walls attenuate the sound of the traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 厚墙削弱了交通的声响。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to make thin': a strong thing is drawn out until it has less body, and less body means less force.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「使变薄」：强的东西被拉长到body更少，而更少的分量就意味着更小的力量。

senses.title: Signal loss along a path
senses.definition: to reduce the strength of an electrical or acoustic signal
senses.definitionCN: 降低电信号或声信号的强度
senses.example: The cable attenuates the signal over long distances.
senses.exampleCN: 电缆在长距离上削弱信号。
senses.why: A signal is a wave carrying energy; as the wave spreads, the same energy covers more space and each point receives less.
senses.whyCN: 信号是携带动能的波；波扩散时同样的能量覆盖更大空间，每一点接收到的就更少。

senses.title: Make thin or tapered
senses.definition: to make something slender, or to draw it out until it narrows
senses.definitionCN: 使某物变细长，或把它拉长到逐渐变窄
senses.example: The glassblower attenuated the neck of the flask.
senses.exampleCN: 吹玻璃的工匠把瓶颈拉细。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense: the object keeps its material but loses its thickness.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的物理义：物体保留材质，却失去厚度。

senses.title: Weaken a pathogen
senses.definition: to reduce the virulence of a microorganism so it can be used in a vaccine
senses.definitionCN: 降低微生物的毒性，使其可用于疫苗
senses.example: Scientists attenuated the virus to make a safe vaccine.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家使病毒减毒，以制造安全的疫苗。
senses.why: A virus that has lost its sharp edge can still teach the body its shape without causing the disease.
senses.whyCN: 失去锋芒的病毒仍能让身体记住它的形状，却不会引发疾病。

senses.title: Make a sound fainter
senses.definition: to reduce the volume or clarity of a sound
senses.definitionCN: 降低声音的音量或清晰度
senses.example: Heavy curtains attenuated the music from the street.
senses.exampleCN: 厚重的窗帘减弱了街上的音乐声。
senses.why: Sound is a pressure wave; a heavy curtain absorbs part of the energy, so the wave arrives with less push.
senses.whyCN: 声音是压力波；厚重窗帘吸收部分能量，因此波到达时推力更小。

senses.title: Water down an idea
senses.definition: to make a statement, argument or proposal less forceful
senses.definitionCN: 使陈述、论证或提议的力度变小
senses.example: The lawyer tried to attenuate the impact of the confession.
senses.exampleCN: 律师试图减弱这份供词的影响。
senses.why: An argument is strength of claim; to attenuate it is to draw the claim thin until it no longer presses.
senses.whyCN: 论证就是主张的力度；削弱它就是把它抽薄，直到不再压人。

senses.title: Reduce risk or harm
senses.definition: to lower the likelihood or severity of harm
senses.definitionCN: 降低伤害发生的可能或严重程度
senses.example: Early warning systems attenuate the damage of storms.
senses.exampleCN: 早期预警系统减轻风暴造成的损失。
senses.why: A warning acts before the event, so it removes some of the energy that the harm would otherwise carry.
senses.whyCN: 预警在事件之前起作用，因此它移除了伤害原本会携带的一部分能量。

senses.title: Fade with distance
senses.definition: to become weaker as it spreads through a medium
senses.definitionCN: 在介质中扩散时逐渐变弱
senses.example: The scent attenuated as we walked away from the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 我们离开花园后，香气渐渐变淡。
senses.why: A scent is particles spreading outward; the further they spread, the fewer reach any one point.
senses.whyCN: 气味是向外扩散的微粒；扩散得越远，到达任一点的就越多。

intro.en: Attenuate is built from a Latin verb for thinning, and the same root gives tenuous.
intro.cn: attenuate 由一个意为「使变薄」的拉丁动词构成，同一个词根产生了 tenuous。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the 16c. for making things thin, and modern technical writing uses it for signals, risks and vaccines.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，表示使变薄；现代技术文本用它指信号、风险与疫苗。

items.en: Attenuare meant 'to make thin, lessen, weaken', formed from ad- 'to' and tenuis 'thin'.
items.cn: attenuare 意为「使变薄、减少、削弱」，由 ad-「向」与 tenuis「薄」构成。

items.en: Tenuis meant 'thin, fine, slight', and also gave English tenuous and the musical term tenor through related forms.
items.cn: tenuis 意为「薄、细、轻微」，也通过相关形式产生英语 tenuous 与音乐术语 tenor。

items.en: Physics measures attenuation in decibels; medicine attenuates pathogens to produce live vaccines.
items.cn: 物理学用分贝衡量衰减；医学使病原体减毒以生产活疫苗。

items.en: The physical image of thinning became an abstract one: claims, risks and feelings can all be drawn thin.
items.cn: 「变薄」的物理形象变成抽象形象：主张、风险与情感都可以被抽薄。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the thinning root or the same derived forms; the near-meaning group names ways of making something less.
note.cn: 形近组共享「变薄」词根或同一派生形式；近义组列出使某物变小的各种方式。

entries.definition: the act or amount of weakening or thinning.
entries.definitionCN: 削弱或变细的行为或程度。

entries.definition: weakened, especially of a virus used in a vaccine.
entries.definitionCN: 被削弱的，尤指疫苗中所用的病毒。

entries.definition: a device that reduces signal strength.
entries.definitionCN: 降低信号强度的装置。

entries.definition: thin, slight and weak, from the same Latin tenuis.
entries.definitionCN: 薄、细微而脆弱，来自同一个拉丁词 tenuis。

entries.definition: to make or become less strong.
entries.definitionCN: 使或变得不那么强。

entries.definition: to make or become smaller in size or importance.
entries.definitionCN: 使在规模或重要性上变小。

entries.definition: to make a liquid weaker by adding water or another fluid.
entries.definitionCN: 加水或其他液体使液体变淡。

entries.definition: to make something harmful less severe.
entries.definitionCN: 使有害之事不那么严重。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a thing drawn thin until its force drops.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「东西被抽薄直到力量下降」的画面留住。

normal.en: Think tenuis, Latin for thin: attenuate means to make thin in body or force.
normal.cn: 想想拉丁语 tenuis「薄」：attenuate 就是让实体或力量变薄。

normal.en: Picture a rope pulled longer and longer until it is a thread.
normal.cn: 想象一根绳子被越拉越长，最后成了一根细线。

normal.en: A signal that fades along a cable is being attenuated by the cable itself.
normal.cn: 沿电缆逐渐变弱的信号，正是被电缆本身衰减。

normal.en: A vaccine virus is attenuated: it keeps the shape but loses the sting.
normal.cn: 疫苗里的病毒是减毒的：保留形状，失去刺痛。

normal.en: Say the word as at-TEN-u-ate, with the thin root in the middle.
normal.cn: 读成 at-TEN-u-ate，中间正是「薄」的词根。

abstract.en: Less body means less force, whether the body is a rope, a wave or a claim.
abstract.cn: 实体更少就意味着力量更小，无论这个实体是绳子、波还是主张。

abstract.en: Reducing a risk works like thinning a wave before it reaches the shore.
abstract.cn: 降低风险就像在波浪抵达岸边之前把它削薄。

abstract.en: What is attenuated still exists, only with less power to act.
abstract.cn: 被削弱之物仍然存在，只是行动的力量更小。

examples.en: Thick walls attenuate the sound of the traffic.

examples.en: Scientists attenuated the virus to make a safe vaccine.
examples.cn: 科学家使病毒减毒，以制造安全的疫苗。

examples.en: The lawyer tried to attenuate the impact of the confession.
examples.cn: 律师试图减弱这份供词的影响。

branches.en: Claims and arguments drawn thin until they stop pressing.
branches.cn: 被抽薄到不再压人的主张与论证。

definition_zh: v. 拘留；扣留；耽搁；留住（使不能离开）
definition_en: to keep someone in a place by official power, or to make them late by keeping them from leaving
core_image: 派出所的钟指向深夜，一个人坐在长椅上不能走；门口有人被礼貌地拦下寒暄
scene: 警方拘留了两名嫌疑人。 Police detained two suspects.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：detained 指拘留；句意是警方拘留了两名嫌疑人。

senses.title: Hold by authority
senses.definition: to keep someone in a place by official power, especially the police
senses.definitionCN: 凭官方权力（尤指警方）把某人留在某处
senses.example: Police detained two suspects.
senses.exampleCN: 警方拘留了两名嫌疑人。
senses.why: A bench in a police room under a late clock.
senses.whyCN: 派出所里一座长椅，上方时钟已晚。

senses.title: Delay on the way
senses.definition: to make someone late by keeping them somewhere
senses.definitionCN: 把某人留在某处而使其迟到
senses.example: We were detained by the traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 我们被交通耽搁了。
senses.why: A car stopped at a closed level crossing.
senses.whyCN: 一辆车停在关闭的铁路道口前。

senses.title: Keep someone talking
senses.definition: to keep someone from leaving, often politely
senses.definitionCN: （常出于礼貌）不让某人离开
senses.example: She detained him at the door with questions.
senses.exampleCN: 她在门口用问题留住了他。
senses.why: A guest in a doorway with a coat half on.
senses.whyCN: 门口一位外套只穿了一半的客人。

intro.en: Detain comes from Latin detinere, de- back plus tenere to hold, and reached English through Old French detenir.
intro.cn: detain 源自拉丁语 detinere，由 de-（扣住）加 tenere（握住）构成，经古法语 detenir 进入英语。

items.en: Tenere meant to hold.
items.cn: tenere 意为握住、持有。

items.en: Detinere meant to hold back.
items.cn: detinere 意为扣住不放。

items.en: Detenir carried the sense into French.
items.cn: 古法语 detenir 承接了这个意思。

items.en: Detain entered English for keeping someone back.
items.cn: 十五世纪 detain 以留住某人义进入英语。

items.en: It gained the legal sense of custody.
items.cn: 十七世纪获得法律上的拘留义。

items.en: Detainee now names the person held.
items.cn: 如今 detainee 指被拘留的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ten- hold family; the near-meaning group names other ways of keeping someone back.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ten-（握住）家族；近义组是其他表示「扣住、留住」的词。

entries.definition: To keep something you already have; it shares tenere but keeps rather than holds back.
entries.definitionCN: 保留已有之物；共享 tenere，但是留住而非扣住。

entries.definition: To hold something inside; it shares tenere but concerns what is inside.
entries.definitionCN: 容纳；共享 tenere，但关乎内部装了什么。

entries.definition: The state of being kept in custody, or a school punishment.
entries.definitionCN: 被拘留的状态，或学校留堂处分。

entries.definition: To make something happen later than planned.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事比计划晚发生。

entries.definition: To keep someone or something in a position.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人或某物保持在某位置。

entries.definition: To keep someone within limits or in a place.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人限制在一定范围或某处。

normalIntro.en: Detain is de- back plus ten- hold: hold someone back so they cannot go on.
normalIntro.cn: detain 就是 de-（扣住）加 ten-（握住）：把人扣住，让他走不了。

normal.en: Ten- means hold, as in tenant.
normal.cn: ten- 意为握住，如 tenant。

normal.en: Detain is what police do to a suspect.
normal.cn: detain 是警方对嫌疑人做的事。

normal.en: Detention is the noun, detainee the person.
normal.cn: detention 是名词，detainee 是被扣的人。

normal.en: Detained by traffic means made late.
normal.cn: detained by traffic 就是被堵车耽搁。

normal.en: Retain keeps, detain holds back.
normal.cn: retain 是保留，detain 是扣住。

abstract.en: A bench in a police room under a late clock.

abstract.cn: 一辆车停在关闭的铁路道口前。

abstract.en: A guest in a doorway with a coat half on.
abstract.cn: 门口一位外套只穿了一半的客人。

examples.cn: 他被扣留了六个小时。

examples.en: The storm detained us at the airport.
examples.cn: 风暴把我们困在机场。

examples.en: Do not detain the witness any longer.
examples.cn: 不要再留住这位证人了。

dict_mnemonic.text: detain ＝ de（扣住、往下）＋ tain（握住，与 contain、retain 同根拉丁语 tenere）＝把人握住不放，「拘留、耽搁」。

root: 拉丁语 tenere（握住）→ de-＋tenere → detinere（扣住）→ 古法语 detenir → 英语 detain

sensesIntro.en: One person kept from going: a bench, a crossing and a doorway.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个走不了的人：一座长椅、一个道口与一处门口。

core.cn: 核心意象：派出所里一座长椅，上方时钟已过了午夜

branches.en: A bench in a police room under a late clock.
branches.cn: 派出所里一座长椅，上方时钟已晚。

branches.en: A car stopped at a closed level crossing.
branches.cn: 一辆车停在关闭的铁路道口前。

branches.en: A guest in a doorway with a coat half on.
branches.cn: 门口一位外套只穿了一半的客人。

branches.en: Both stop someone reaching where they meant to go.
branches.cn: 两者都让人到不了原本要去的地方。

branches.en: Both cost the person time.
branches.cn: 两者都耗掉了这个人的时间。

intro.en: Detain is de- plus ten-; the hold root also builds retain, contain and tenant.
intro.cn: detain 由 de- 加 ten- 构成；握住这个词根也造出 retain、contain 与 tenant。

latinIntro.en: Latin tenere means to hold, mora a delay and finis a limit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tenere 意为握住，mora 意为迟延，finis 意为界限。

definition_zh: 使康复；使恢复功能；改造罪犯使之重返社会；恢复名誉、权利或职位；使建筑物、生态恢复良好状态
definition_en: to restore a person to health, ability or a normal place in society, or to bring something back into good condition
core_image: 康复室里，病人双手扶着平行杠重新学迈步，治疗师在旁护着腰
scene: 事故之后，那名木工半年上不了脚手架，康复中心替他排了一套从抬腿到负重的训练。 The clinic designed a slow programme to rehabilitate the injured carpenter.
sceneCN: 这里指「通过训练使伤者重新恢复身体功能」，对应第 2 个义项：借助治疗与反复练习，把失去的动作能力一点点建回来；句意为康复中心为受伤的木工安排了一套循序渐进的训练。画面要点：平行杠、治疗师、重新迈出的第一步。

pos.zh: 使康复；改造；恢复（及物动词，宾语可为人、机构、建筑或生态）

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表动作或结果）→ 由「使恢复能力」转为「康复、复权的整个过程」
加形容词后缀（表倾向或功能）→ 由「使恢复」转为「有助于康复的」
加过去分词词尾（转作形容词）→ 由「已使恢复」转为「已康复或已恢复资格的」
由拉丁词干（源自 habilis「能干的」）加动词词尾（源自拉丁语，表「使……」）→ 由「能干」转为「使具备能力、使合用」
habilitate 加名词后缀（表动作或结果）→ 由「使有能力」转为「取得资格的过程」
源自拉丁 habilis「易于掌握的、能干的」加名词后缀（表性质）→ 由「能干」转为「能力」这一性质

senses.title: Back to health: a sick body made well
senses.titleCN: 让病后的身体回到健康
senses.definition: to bring a person back to health after illness or injury through care and treatment
senses.definitionCN: 通过照料与治疗，使人在患病或受伤之后恢复健康
senses.example: The team worked for months to rehabilitate patients after the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 团队工作了数月，帮助火灾后的病人康复。
senses.why: The prefix re- means 'again, back', and the Latin base means 'to make able', so the core is not punishment but the return of a capacity that had been lost.
senses.whyCN: 前缀表示「再、回」，拉丁词干意为「使有能力」，因此这个词的核心不是惩罚，而是让一项失去的能力回来。

senses.title: Retraining a joint or limb: step by step
senses.titleCN: 一点一点练回关节与肢体
senses.definition: to train a specific movement or faculty until it works again
senses.definitionCN: 针对某一动作或机能反复训练，直到它重新正常工作
senses.example: She practised daily to rehabilitate her injured shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天练习，让受伤的肩膀恢复功能。
senses.why: The capacity is concrete: a shoulder, a knee, a step. The verb then names the slow drill that brings the movement back rather than the abstract idea of health.
senses.whyCN: 这里的能力很具体：一个肩膀、一只膝盖、一步路。动词因此指把这动作练回来的缓慢训练，而不是抽象的健康概念。

senses.title: Reform for society: not merely punish
senses.titleCN: 为重返社会而改造，而非只加惩罚
senses.definition: to prepare a convicted person for ordinary life through education, work and treatment rather than mere punishment
senses.definitionCN: 以教育、劳动与治疗帮助已定罪者过普通生活，而不是只施加惩罚
senses.example: The prison runs classes to rehabilitate young offenders.
senses.exampleCN: 这所监狱开设课程，帮助少年犯改过自新。
senses.why: A person who has lost their place in society is treated like a person who has lost a function: the task is to restore the ability to live among others, not to add pain.
senses.whyCN: 失去社会位置的人，被当作失去一项功能的人来处理：任务是恢复他与别人共同生活的能力，而不是增加痛苦。

senses.title: Rights and name restored: the legal sense
senses.titleCN: 恢复权利与名誉的法律义
senses.definition: to give a person back a former legal standing, office or good name
senses.definitionCN: 把某人原先的法律地位、职位或名誉归还给他
senses.example: The decree rehabilitated the officers who had been dismissed.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法令为那些被免职的军官恢复了名誉。
senses.why: This is the oldest use: re- means back, and the person is returned to a position that had been taken away, so the word speaks of standing rather than of the body.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的用法：前缀意为「回」，人被送回一个曾被剥夺的位置，因此这个词讲的是地位，而不是身体。

senses.title: Bricks made usable: buildings brought back
senses.definition: to repair and upgrade a building, district or facility so that it is usable again
senses.definitionCN: 修缮并提升建筑、街区或设施，使其重新可以使用
senses.example: The city plans to rehabilitate the old dock warehouses.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府计划修缮旧码头的仓库。
senses.why: The object shifts from a body to bricks, but the shape of the act is the same: something fallen into disrepair is made fit for use again.
senses.whyCN: 对象从身体换成了砖块，但动作的形状没变：一样陷入失修的东西被重新弄得合于使用。

senses.title: Land healed: an ecosystem restored
senses.titleCN: 让土地与生态恢复健康
senses.definition: to return damaged land, water or habitat to a healthy working state
senses.definitionCN: 使受损的土地、水体或栖息地回到健康的运转状态
senses.example: Volunteers rehabilitated the strip mine into a wetland.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者把露天矿坑修复成了湿地。
senses.why: Land, too, can lose its functions; the verb treats soil and water as a system whose capacities must be brought back, just as a body's are.
senses.whyCN: 土地也会失去它的功能；这个动词把土壤与水当作一套必须把能力恢复过来的系统，正如对待身体一样。

senses.title: Back in the post: an official reinstated
senses.titleCN: 让官员回到原来的职位
senses.definition: to restore an official to a post, rank or privilege that had been removed
senses.definitionCN: 使官员回到曾被撤销的职位、军衔或特权
senses.example: The board voted to rehabilitate the suspended director.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会投票决定恢复被停职董事的职位。
senses.why: When the lost thing is a seat at the table, the verb moves from bodily capacity to institutional membership, yet the 'making able again' remains.
senses.whyCN: 当失去的东西是桌边的一个席位，这个词就从身体能力转向制度中的成员资格，但「重新使有能力」这一层仍然在。

senses.title: A good name regained: ideas and works
senses.titleCN: 让作品与观念重获好评
senses.definition: to make a neglected or discredited idea, word or artwork respected again
senses.definitionCN: 使被冷落或已被否定的观念、词语或作品重新受到尊重
senses.example: Later critics rehabilitated the painter's early work.
senses.exampleCN: 后来的评论家为这位画家早期的作品恢复了声誉。
senses.why: Reputation is another capacity that can be lost, and the verb extends to anything whose good name has been taken away, from a person to a painting.
senses.whyCN: 声誉也是一种会失去的能力，这个词于是扩展到任何被夺去好评的东西，从一个人到一幅画都可以。

intro.en: Rehabilitate is not a native English construction: it comes from Medieval Latin rehabilitare, itself re- 'again, back' plus habilitare 'to make able', a verb from habilis 'apt, easily handled'. The same family contains ability and habilitate. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: rehabilitate 不是英语本土构造，而来自中世纪拉丁 rehabilitare：由表示「再、回」的前缀加 habilitare「使有能力」构成，后者又出自 habilis「易于掌握的、能干的」；同一词族还有 ability 与 habilitate。年代均为约数。

items.en: Habilis meant apt, handy or easily handled, an adjective built on habere 'to hold'; the idea was fitness for use.
items.cn: habilis 意为易于掌握的、顺手的、能干的，是由 habere「持有」构成的形容词，核心意思是「合用」。

items.en: Habilitare turned the adjective into a verb meaning to make able or to fit something for a purpose.
items.cn: habilitare 把这个形容词变成动词，意为使有能力，或使某物适合某一用途。

items.en: Re- 'again, back' was added to habilitare, and the compound was used in law and church language for restoring a person to a former right or rank.
items.cn: 表示「再、回」的前缀加在 habilitare 上，这个复合词用于法律与教会语言，指把某人恢复到原有的权利或地位。

items.en: English took the word in the sixteenth century, first in legal and ecclesiastical use for restoring standing.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收了这个词，最初用于法律与教会语境，指恢复地位。

items.en: The medical and social senses developed later: restoring a patient's body, then preparing an offender for ordinary life.
items.cn: 医学与社会义后来才发展出来：先指恢复病人的身体，再指为罪犯重返普通生活作准备。

items.en: Contemporary usage extends the verb to buildings, districts, ecosystems and the reputation of ideas or works.
items.cn: 当代用法把这个动词扩展到建筑、街区、生态系统，以及观念或作品的声誉。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin ability stem or merely resembles the word in spelling; the second group offers near alternatives for bringing something back to a good state.
note.cn: 第一组或与本词共享拉丁「能力」词干，或只是拼写相近；第二组是「把某物带回良好状态」的近义替代。

entries.definition: To make someone able or fit; it is the base verb without the 'again' prefix, so it lacks the idea of restoring something already lost.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人有能力或合于用途；这是去掉「再」这一前缀的底层动词，因此不含「把已失去之物恢复过来」的意思。

entries.definition: To make someone weak; it is built on the same Latin ability adjective but through a prefix of removal, so it undoes capacity instead of restoring it.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人衰弱；它由同一个拉丁「能力」形容词经表「去除」的前缀构成，因此是拆掉能力而非恢复能力。

entries.definition: To sum up the main points again; it shares the re- prefix and the -ate ending but comes from Latin caput 'head', so it is merely look-alike, not a relative.
entries.definitionCN: 再次概括要点；它与本词共享「再」这一前缀和动词词尾，但出自拉丁 caput「头」，只是形近，并非同源。

entries.definition: The informal short form of rehabilitation, used chiefly for treatment programmes and centres.
entries.definitionCN: rehabilitation 的口语缩略形式，主要用于治疗项目与康复中心。

entries.definition: To bring something back to a former condition; it is broader and does not specify ability, health or standing.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物带回原先的状态；范围更宽，不特别指明能力、健康或地位。

entries.definition: To put a person back into a post or right; it covers only the institutional sense of the word.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人放回职位或权利之中；只覆盖本词的制度义。

entries.definition: To bring a person back into a group or society; it names the social goal rather than the training that achieves it.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人带回群体或社会之中；它指社会目标，而不是达成目标的训练。

entries.definition: To improve a person or institution by removing faults; for offenders it stresses moral change, while this word stresses restored capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 通过去除毛病来改善人或制度；用于罪犯时强调品德转变，而本词强调能力的恢复。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin ability stem, the real 'again' prefix and real derived words such as ability and habilitate.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「能力」词干、真实的「再」前缀，以及 ability、habilitate 等真实派生词。

normal.en: Habilis means apt or able, and the English word ability comes from the same Latin adjective.
normal.cn: habilis 意为能干的、合用的，英语 ability 正出自同一个拉丁形容词。

normal.en: The prefix re- means again or back, so the word says the ability is brought back.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「再、回」，所以这个词说的是把能力带回来。

normal.en: Habilitate is the base verb 'to make able'; rehabilitate adds the return to a former state.
normal.cn: habilitate 是底层动词「使有能力」，rehabilitate 则再加「回到原先状态」这一层。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the range: rehabilitate offenders, rehabilitate a building, drug rehabilitation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配展现范围：改造罪犯、修缮建筑、戒毒康复。

normal.en: The noun rehabilitation and the adjective rehabilitative both keep the idea of making fit again.
normal.cn: 名词 rehabilitation 与形容词 rehabilitative 都保留「重新弄得合用」这一意思。

abstract.en: Picture a patient gripping parallel bars and lifting one foot again.
abstract.cn: 想象病人握住平行杠，再一次把一只脚抬起来。

abstract.en: Picture a released prisoner handed a work badge at a factory gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一名获释的服刑人员在工厂门口接过工牌。

abstract.en: Picture a ruined brick warehouse with fresh scaffolding around it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座破败的砖砌仓库四周搭起了新的脚手架。

examples.en: Therapy helped rehabilitate her knee after the operation.
examples.cn: 治疗帮助她的膝盖在手术后恢复功能。

examples.en: Programmes that rehabilitate offenders cost less than long sentences.
examples.cn: 改造罪犯的项目比长期监禁花费更少。

examples.en: The trust hopes to rehabilitate the discredited theory with new evidence.
examples.cn: 该基金会希望用新证据为这个已被否定的理论恢复声誉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞哈比立忒」——瑞气回来，比着平行杠把腿立起来，人又能站直了 → 康复、复权

root: 拉丁语表「回、再」的前缀 + habilitare「使有能力」（← habilis「易于掌握的、能干的」← habere「持有」）→ 中世纪拉丁 rehabilitare「使恢复能力与资格」；同族词有 ability、habilitate、rehabilitation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep the same movement: something that once had a capacity lost it, and the verb brings that capacity back. The capacity may be health, a movement, a place in society, a legal right, a building's usefulness, a landscape's fertility, a post or a good name.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项守着同一个动作：某样东西本来具有一项能力，后来失去了，这个动词把它带回来。这项能力可以是健康、一个动作、社会位置、法律权利、建筑的可用性、土地的生机、一个职位，或一份好评。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands on parallel bars, one foot lifted again after a long pause.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手扶住平行杠，停歇很久之后那只脚又一次抬起来。

branches.en: THE BODY: health returns first as a general condition, then as a single joint or step trained back into use.
branches.cn: 身体：健康先以整体状态回来，随后又以某个关节或某一步被练回可用。

branches.en: THE PLACE AMONG OTHERS: an offender is fitted for ordinary life, and an official is put back into a lost post.
branches.cn: 人群中的位置：让罪犯重新适合普通生活，也让官员回到失去的职位。

branches.en: THE LEGAL NAME: rights and reputation are handed back by formal decision.
branches.cn: 法律上的名分：权利与名誉经正式决定被归还。

branches.en: THE MADE WORLD: bricks and land are repaired until they can work again.
branches.cn: 人造与自然之物：砖石与土地被修整到能重新运转。

branches.en: THE GOOD NAME OF THINGS: even a discredited idea or artwork can be given its standing back.
branches.cn: 事物的好评：连一个被否定的观念或作品，也能重新得到它应有的地位。

intro.en: Rehabilitate is assembled from Latin pieces: a prefix of return, an adjective stem meaning able, and a verb ending, with English noun and adjective suffixes added later.
intro.cn: rehabilitate 由拉丁成分拼成：一个表示「回、再」的前缀、一个意为「能干」的形容词词干，以及一个动词词尾；英语的名词与形容词后缀是后来才加上去的。

latinIntro.en: Latin habilis 'apt' came from habere 'to hold', and it also produced habilitare, rehabilitare and the English word ability.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 habilis「合用的、能干的」出自 habere「持有」，它还衍生出 habilitare、rehabilitare 以及英语的 ability。

items.meaning: again; back to a former state
items.example: The prefix marks the return of something that was lost.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出「失去之物重新回来」。

items.example: The stem describes a person or thing that can be handled well.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干描述一个人或物能被好好使用。

items.structure: stem of Latin habilitare (to make able)
items.example: The stem carries the act of fitting someone for a task.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载「使人适合某项任务」的动作。

items.meaning: to make; to cause to be
items.meaningCN: 使成为；使处于某种状态
items.example: The ending marks the word as a verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把该词标为动词。

items.example: The clinic aims to rehabilitate each patient.
items.exampleCN: 康复中心的目标是让每位病人恢复功能。

items.example: Rehabilitation takes many months after a severe injury.
items.exampleCN: 重伤之后康复需要许多个月。
该病区提供康复性照护。

items.example: The rehabilitated building reopened as a school.
items.exampleCN: 修缮后的建筑作为学校重新开放。

items.meaning: the process of making someone able
items.exampleCN: 先具备能力，才能独立工作。

items.example: The injury did not damage her ability to walk.
items.exampleCN: 这次受伤没有损害她行走的能力。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 合用的；易于掌握的；能干的

latinEntries.meaning: to restore to a former right or capacity
latinEntries.meaningCN: 恢复原有的权利或能力

definition_zh: n. 失职；过失；（尤指青少年的）违法行为；拖欠
definition_en: failure to do a duty, or minor crime, especially by young people
core_image: 值班表上有一格空着，负责人没来，桌上的记录本停在昨天
scene: 青少年违法率今年下降了。 Juvenile delinquency fell this year.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：delinquency 指违法行为；句意是青少年违法率今年下降了。

pos.zh: 失职；过失；（尤指青少年的）违法行为；拖欠

derivatives.zh: 失职的；有过失的；违法的

senses.title: Failure of duty
senses.definition: failure to do what a duty or a job requires
senses.definitionCN: 没有做到职责或工作要求的事
senses.example: The audit found delinquency in the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 审计发现夜班存在失职。
senses.why: An empty square on a duty roster.
senses.whyCN: 值班表上的一格空白。

senses.title: Minor crime
senses.definition: minor crime, especially when committed by young people
senses.definitionCN: 轻微的犯罪行为，尤指青少年所为
senses.example: Juvenile delinquency fell this year.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年违法率今年下降了。
senses.why: A broken shop window and a bored teenager.
senses.whyCN: 一扇被打碎的橱窗和一个无聊的少年。

senses.title: Overdue payment
senses.definition: the state of a payment that is late or still unpaid
senses.definitionCN: 款项逾期或未付的状态
senses.example: The bank tracks loan delinquency each month.
senses.exampleCN: 银行每月跟踪贷款拖欠情况。
senses.why: A calendar page with a red overdue stamp.
senses.whyCN: 一页盖着红色逾期章的日历。

intro.en: Delinquency comes from Latin delinquere, de- plus linquere, to leave: a duty left undone.
intro.cn: delinquency 源自拉丁语 delinquere，由 de- 加 linquere（留下）构成：把职责留下不做。

items.en: Linquere meant to leave or let go.
items.cn: linquere 意为离开、放手。

items.en: Delinquere meant to leave a duty undone, to fail.
items.cn: delinquere 意为把职责留下不做，即失职。

items.en: Delinquentia named the failing or the fault.
items.cn: delinquentia 指失职或过失。

items.en: Delinquency entered English for neglect of duty.
items.cn: 十七世纪 delinquency 以玩忽职守义进入英语。

items.en: It came to name minor offences by the young.
items.cn: 十九世纪转而指青少年的轻微犯罪。

definition_zh: 提取；开采；拔除；摘录；出身
definition_en: the act of drawing something out of a place, a substance, a body or a text
core_image: 一根吸管插进果肉，把里面的汁一点点抽出来
scene: 这里指「提取」。 DNA extraction from the sample took less than an hour with the new kit.
sceneCN: 这里 extraction 是「提取」（第 1 个义项：把某物质从混合物或样本中分离出来）；句意：用新试剂盒从样本中提取 DNA 不到一小时。图中可辨识物件：离心管、移液枪、试剂盒、样本。

pos.zh: 提取；开采；拔除；摘录；出身

senses.title: Drawing a substance out
senses.titleCN: 提取：把想要的东西从混合物里分离
senses.definition: the chemical or physical process of separating a substance from a mixture or sample
senses.definitionCN: 从混合物或样本中分离出某物质的化学或物理过程
senses.example: The extraction of caffeine from coffee beans uses a solvent and heat.
senses.exampleCN: 从咖啡豆中提取咖啡因要用溶剂和加热。
senses.why: extrahere means 'to draw out'. Extraction names the process after the direction: what is wanted is pulled out of what surrounds it.
senses.whyCN: extrahere 意为“抽出”。extraction 按方向命名过程：想要的东西被从包围它的东西里拉出来。

senses.title: Taking ore from the ground
senses.titleCN: 开采：把矿从地下取出来
senses.definition: the mining of coal, oil, gas or minerals from the earth
senses.definitionCN: 从地下开采煤、石油、天然气或矿物
senses.example: Coal extraction in the region fell by a third in ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的煤炭开采量十年间下降了三分之一。
senses.why: Mining is the same pull, only the container is the earth. The word treats the ground as a substance from which something is drawn.
senses.whyCN: 采矿是同一种“拉”，只是容器变成了大地。这个词把地面当作一种可以被抽出东西的物质。

senses.title: Pulling a tooth or a bullet
senses.titleCN: 拔除：把嵌在身体里的东西取出来
senses.definition: the removal of a tooth, bullet or other object from the body
senses.definitionCN: 从身体中取出牙齿、子弹或其他物体
senses.example: The extraction of the damaged tooth took only fifteen minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 拔掉那颗坏牙只用了十五分钟。
senses.why: Dentistry uses extraction because the tooth is embedded in the gum. The object is not cut away; it is drawn out whole.
senses.whyCN: 牙科用 extraction，因为牙齿嵌在牙龈里。不是把牙削掉，而是整颗抽出来。

senses.title: A passage taken from a text
senses.titleCN: 摘录：从文章里抽一段出来
senses.definition: a short passage copied out of a longer text
senses.definitionCN: 从较长文本中抄出的一段短文
senses.example: The anthology prints an extraction from her 1897 diary.
senses.exampleCN: 这本选集刊出了她 1897 年日记的一段摘录。
senses.why: Here the container is a book. The image holds: a piece is pulled out and shown apart from the whole that held it.
senses.whyCN: 这里的容器是一本书。意象不变：一块内容被抽出来，脱离原本包住它的整体单独展示。

senses.title: Origin or descent
senses.titleCN: 出身：从哪个家族抽出来的
senses.definition: a person's family origin or social background, used in the phrase 'of ... extraction'
senses.definitionCN: 某人的家族出身或社会背景，用于 of ... extraction 这一说法
senses.example: She is of Italian extraction but grew up in Buenos Aires.
senses.exampleCN: 她是意大利裔，但在布宜诺斯艾利斯长大。
senses.why: The figurative sense treats ancestry as the substance a person was drawn from. You come out of a family the way a filament is pulled from a source.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻义把血统当作人被抽出的“原料”。人出自某个家族，就像细丝从源头被抽出。

senses.title: Pulling data out
senses.titleCN: 数据提取：从系统里抽调信息
senses.definition: the process of retrieving selected information from records, websites or databases
senses.definitionCN: 从记录、网页或数据库中取回选定信息的过程
senses.example: Automated extraction turned ten thousand invoices into a single table.
senses.exampleCN: 自动提取把一万张发票变成了一张表。
senses.why: Databases are the modern ore. The verb stays exact: the wanted rows are drawn out of the mass that stores them.
senses.whyCN: 数据库是现代矿石。动词仍精确：想要的行被从储存它们的大堆数据里抽出来。

senses.title: How much comes out
senses.definition: the proportion of a useful substance recovered from the raw material
senses.definitionCN: 从原料中回收的有用物质所占比例
senses.example: The new press raised the oil extraction rate from 18 to 24 percent.
senses.exampleCN: 新压榨机把出油率从 18% 提高到 24%。
senses.why: Once the process is named, the result can be measured. Extraction rate simply asks how much of the target actually left its container.
senses.whyCN: 过程一旦被命名，结果就能被计量。extraction rate 问的就是目标物实际离开了容器多少。

senses.title: Forcing out a confession
senses.titleCN: 逼取：把口供从人嘴里抽出来
senses.definition: the act of obtaining money or information from someone by pressure or threat
senses.definitionCN: 通过施压或威胁从某人处取得钱财或信息
senses.example: The report condemned the extraction of confessions under threat.
senses.exampleCN: 报告谴责在威胁下逼取口供的做法。
senses.why: This darker sense uses the same verb on a person: information is treated as something held inside and pulled out by force.
senses.whyCN: 这个更黑暗的义项把同一动词用在人身上：信息被当作藏在体内、靠强力抽出的东西。

intro.en: Extraction comes from extract, from Latin extrahere 'to draw out', built on ex- 'out' plus trahere 'to draw, drag'. The word has always been about direction: something is pulled from its container.
intro.cn: extraction 来自 extract，而 extract 出自拉丁 extrahere“抽出”，由 ex-“向外”加 trahere“拉、拖”构成。这个词始终关于方向：某物被从容器里拉出来。

items.en: trahere meant 'to draw, drag, pull'. Its past participle tractus gives English tract, tractor and contract; the same root underlies attract and distract with different prefixes.
items.cn: trahere 意为“拉、拖、拽”。其过去分词 tractus 生出英语 tract、tractor、contract；同一词根也见于 attract、distract，但前缀不同。

items.en: ex- 'out' plus trahere gives extrahere 'to draw out'. The verb pictured a hand pulling something from a bag or a body.
items.cn: ex-“向外”加 trahere 构成 extrahere“抽出”。这个动词原画面是一只手从袋子或身体里往外拉东西。

items.en: The past participle extractus 'drawn out' becomes the source of the English noun and adjective extract. The thing pulled out could be a passage, a metal or a essence.
items.cn: 过去分词 extractus“被抽出的”成为英语名词与形容词 extract 的来源。被抽出的东西可以是段落、金属或精华。

items.en: English forms extraction on extract plus -ion, from Latin -io, naming the action. The word appears in the 15th century in alchemy and medicine.
items.cn: 英语以 extract 加 -ion（来自拉丁 -io，命名动作）构成 extraction。该词 15 世纪见于炼金术与医学。

items.en: From the 18th and 19th centuries extraction spreads to mining and dentistry, where the container is the earth or the jaw.
items.cn: 18 至 19 世纪，extraction 扩展到采矿与牙科，容器变成大地或下颌。

items.en: The data sense is a 20th-century extension; the ancestry sense, 'of Italian extraction', is older and treats family as the source material.
items.cn: 数据义是 20 世纪的扩展；血统义 of Italian extraction 更早，把家族当作原料来源。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tract- stem or the ex- prefix; the near-meaning group all involve taking something out or away, but from different containers.
note.cn: 形近组共享 tract- 词干或 ex- 前缀；近义组都涉及“取出、拿走”，但容器不同。

entries.definition: to draw out, or the substance drawn out. It is the base word; extraction names the action.
entries.definitionCN: 抽出；提取物。它是基础词；extraction 命名动作。

entries.definition: relating to extraction, especially mining and drilling. It describes an industry, not a process step.
entries.definitionCN: 提取的；采掘的，尤指采矿与钻探。它描述产业，不描述某个操作步骤。

entries.definition: the official handing over of a person to another country. It looks close because of extra-, but comes from ex- plus tradere 'hand over', not trahere 'draw'.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人正式移交给另一国。它因 extra- 而形近，但来自 ex- 加 tradere“交出”，并非 trahere“拉”。

entries.definition: the act of taking something away from a place. It is broader than extraction and often implies clearing.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从某处拿走的行为。它比 extraction 宽泛，常含“清理”之意。

entries.definition: the industry of taking coal, metal or gems from the earth. It is the industrial setting of one extraction sense.
entries.definitionCN: 从地下开采煤、金属或宝石的产业。它是 extraction 某一义项的产业场景。

entries.definition: a short piece taken from a book or speech. It is the product, while extraction is the act of taking it.
entries.definitionCN: 从书或讲话中摘取的短段。它是成品，而 extraction 是摘取的动作。

entries.definition: the origin of something, or the process of obtaining it from a source. It overlaps the ancestry sense but sounds more technical.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的来源，或从源头获得的过程。它与“出身”义重叠，但更技术化。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ex- 'out' + trahere 'draw': extraction is the pull that moves something out of its container.
normal.cn: ex-“向外”+ trahere“拉”：extraction 就是把东西从容器里往外拉的那一下。

normal.en: tract, tractor, contract and extraction share the tract- stem, so the family is one memory block.
normal.cn: tract、tractor、contract、extraction 共享 tract- 词干，可整块记忆。

normal.en: tooth extraction is the clearest picture: the tooth is not cut, it is pulled out whole.
normal.cn: tooth extraction 是最清楚的画面：牙不是被削掉，而是整颗被拔出。

normal.en: extraction rate turns the action into a number, which shows how much of the target actually left.
normal.cn: extraction rate 把这个动作变成一个数字，显示目标物实际出来了多少。

normal.en: of Italian extraction uses the same verb for family: a person is drawn from a source.
normal.cn: of Italian extraction 把同一动词用在家族上：人是从某个源头抽出来的。

abstract.en: Think of a syringe drawing liquid from a sealed vial, the level falling as the barrel fills.
abstract.cn: 想象注射器从密封小瓶里抽液，针筒满起来时瓶里的液面下降。

abstract.en: Think of a single page being lifted out of a thick book and laid on a table.
abstract.cn: 想象从一本厚书里抽出一页，单独放在桌上。

abstract.en: Think of a mine shaft as a straw pushed into the ground, with ore rising through it.
abstract.cn: 想象矿井是一根插进地里的吸管，矿石从里面升上来。

examples.en: The lab reports the extraction yield in milligrams per litre.
examples.cn: 实验室以每升多少毫克报告提取产量。

examples.en: After the extraction of the second molar, he ate only soft food for a week.
examples.cn: 拔掉第二磨牙后，他一周只吃软食。

examples.en: The chapter is an extraction from a longer memoir published in 1932.
examples.cn: 这一章摘自 1932 年出版的一部更长回忆录。
