root: 拉丁 extrahere“抽出”（ex-“向外”+ trahere“拉、拖”，过去分词 tractus）；extract + -ion 构成动作名词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one direction: something is pulled out of whatever held it, whether earth, body, book or bloodline.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个方向：某物被从包住它的东西里拉出来，不论是大地、身体、书本还是血统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straw drawing juice out of fruit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根吸管把果汁从果肉里抽出来。

branches.en: SUBSTANCE: chemical extraction and the extraction rate are the same separation seen as process and as measurement.
branches.cn: 物质：化学提取与提取率是同一个分离过程，一个看过程，一个看量度。

branches.en: EARTH: mining treats the ground as the container, with ore drawn upward through the shaft.
branches.cn: 大地：采矿把地面当容器，矿石沿矿井被向上抽出。

branches.en: BODY: a tooth or bullet is drawn out whole rather than cut away.
branches.cn: 身体：牙齿或子弹是整块被拔出，而不是削掉。

branches.en: INFORMATION: a passage and a database row are both selected pieces pulled from a larger store.
branches.cn: 信息：一段文字与一行数据库记录，都是从更大储存中取出的选定片段。

branches.en: SOURCE AND FORCE: ancestry is the source one is drawn from, while a forced confession is pulled out of a person against resistance.
branches.cn: 来源与强力：血统是人被抽出的源头，而逼供是违背抵抗从人身上抽出信息。

intro.en: Extraction is extract plus -ion. The ex- prefix means 'out', the -tract- stem means 'draw', and -ion names the action; -or and -ive build agent and quality nouns.
intro.cn: extraction 是 extract 加 -ion。ex- 前缀意为“向外”，-tract- 词干意为“拉”，-ion 命名动作；-or 与 -ive 构成施事与性质词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family grows from trahere 'draw' through extrahere 'draw out'. English relatives include extract, tractor, contract, attract and distract, each with its own prefix.
latinIntro.cn: 这个拉丁词族从 trahere“拉”经 extrahere“抽出”生长。英语同族词包括 extract、tractor、contract、attract、distract，各自前缀不同。

items.meaning: to draw out; the thing drawn out
items.meaningCN: 抽出；提取物（ex-“向外”+ trahere“拉”）
items.example: The machine extracts oil from the seeds.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器从种子里榨油。

items.meaningCN: 提取；开采（-ion 动作名词）
items.exampleCN: 开采在天亮前就开始了。

items.meaning: a device or person that extracts
items.meaningCN: 提取器；排气扇（-or 施事或器械）
items.example: The kitchen extractor pulls smoke out of the room.
items.exampleCN: 厨房排风扇把烟抽出房间。

items.meaningCN: 提取的；采掘的（-ive 关系形容词）
items.exampleCN: 采掘业在该省占主导地位。

items.example: Only half of the sugar is extractable by this method.
items.exampleCN: 用这种方法只能提取出一半的糖。

items.meaning: a vehicle that draws or pulls implements
items.meaningCN: 拖拉机（tract-“拉”+ -or 施事，同一词根）
items.example: The tractor pulled the plough across the field.
items.exampleCN: 拖拉机拉着犁穿过田地。

items.meaning: to draw together, hence a binding agreement
items.meaningCN: 收缩；合同（con-“共同”+ trahere“拉”，把双方拉到一起）
items.example: The two firms signed a three-year contract.
items.exampleCN: 两家公司签了三年合同。

items.meaning: to draw attention apart; to divert
items.meaningCN: 分散注意力（dis-“分开”+ trahere“拉”）
items.example: The noise distracted the whole class.
items.exampleCN: 噪音分散了全班的注意力。

definition_zh: 急流；高空强而窄的气流带；极地急流；副热带急流
definition_en: a narrow, fast band of wind in the upper troposphere that steers weather systems and aircraft
core_image: 高空一条绷紧的白色卷云带被拉成细长直线，飞机顺着它加速，风暴在它下方被牵着走
scene: 高空那条狭长的高速气流像一根绷紧的绳，把风暴一路牵向东北。 The jet stream steered the storm north-east across the Pacific.
sceneCN: 这里指「对流层上部狭长的高速风带」（第 1 个义项：风速极大、呈带状的上层气流）；句意为急流把风暴引导向东北，横越太平洋。图中可辨识物件：拉长的卷云带、顺流加速的飞机、被牵引的风暴云系、高空流线。

senses.title: A narrow fast band in the upper troposphere
senses.titleCN: 对流层上部狭长的高速风带
senses.definition: a narrow band of very strong wind near the tropopause, marked by sharp horizontal wind shear
senses.definitionCN: 对流层顶附近风力极强、水平风切变明显的狭长风带
senses.example: The jet stream steered the storm north-east across the Pacific.
senses.exampleCN: 急流把风暴引导向东北，横越太平洋。
senses.why: The name joins a fast jet of air to a stream of water: both are narrow, fast and confined.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字把高速气流之「射流」与水流之「溪流」合在一起：两者都窄、都快、都受限。

senses.title: The polar jet stream
senses.definition: the jet stream associated with the polar front, lying between the mid-latitudes and the polar air
senses.definitionCN: 与极锋相关、位于中纬度与极地空气之间的急流
senses.example: The polar jet stream dipped south and brought Arctic air to the plains.
senses.exampleCN: 极地急流南压，把北极空气带到平原。
senses.why: The temperature contrast at the polar front is what concentrates the wind into a narrow core.
senses.whyCN: 极锋处的温差正是把风集中成狭窄核心的原因。

senses.title: The subtropical jet stream
senses.definition: the jet stream found near thirty degrees latitude, linked to the subtropical high and the Hadley circulation
senses.definitionCN: 位于纬度三十度附近、与副热带高压及哈得来环流相关的急流
senses.example: The subtropical jet stream carried moisture toward the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 副热带急流把水汽送向海岸。
senses.why: A second maximum exists where the Hadley cell returns its air aloft, separate from the polar front.
senses.whyCN: 在哈得来环流高空回流处还存在第二个极大值，与极锋无关。

senses.title: The wind that changes flight times
senses.definition: the upper wind whose direction can shorten an eastbound flight or lengthen a westbound one
senses.definitionCN: 其方向可缩短向东航班、延长向西航班的高空风
senses.example: A strong jet stream cut two hours off the eastbound flight.
senses.exampleCN: 强劲的急流使向东航班缩短了两小时。
senses.why: Aircraft fly within the flow, so a following stream adds ground speed and an opposing one subtracts it.
senses.whyCN: 飞机在气流中飞行，顺流增加地速，逆流则减少。

senses.title: A guide for surface weather systems
senses.titleCN: 地面天气系统的引导带
senses.definition: the upper flow that steers cyclones and anticyclones along its path
senses.definitionCN: 沿其路径引导气旋与反气旋移动的上层气流
senses.example: The jet stream turned the depression toward the British Isles.
senses.exampleCN: 急流把低压转向不列颠群岛。
senses.why: Surface lows are steered by the stronger flow above them, so the jet acts as rails.
senses.whyCN: 地面低压被上方更强的气流引导，因此急流起了轨道的作用。

senses.title: Clear-air turbulence
senses.definition: turbulence near the jet stream that occurs without cloud, caused by wind shear
senses.definitionCN: 急流附近无云却由风切变引起的颠簸
senses.example: The crew warned passengers about clear-air turbulence near the jet stream.
senses.exampleCN: 机组提醒乘客急流附近有晴空颠簸。
senses.why: Where fast air meets slower air, the boundary becomes unstable even when the sky looks empty.
senses.whyCN: 当快气流遇到慢气流，即使天空看起来空无一物，边界也会失稳。

senses.title: The seasonal shift of the jet
senses.definition: the poleward shift in summer and equatorward shift in winter of the jet stream's typical position
senses.definitionCN: 急流典型位置在夏季向极地、冬季向赤道的移动
senses.example: The jet stream's seasonal shift decides where the rains arrive.
senses.exampleCN: 急流的季节性移动决定了雨带抵达何处。
senses.why: The temperature contrast that drives the jet moves with the seasons, so the rail moves with it.
senses.whyCN: 驱动急流的温差随季节移动，因此这条轨道也随之移动。

senses.title: A fast, unceasing channel, figuratively
senses.definition: a fast, continuous channel that carries things along with little friction
senses.definitionCN: 把事物低阻力地持续带走的快速通道
senses.example: The city became a jet stream of capital and talent.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市成了一条资金与人才的高速通道。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps speed, narrowness and one-way flow, dropping the meteorology.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻保留速度、狭窄与单向流动，去掉气象内容。

intro.en: Jet stream joins jet, from Old French jeter 'to throw' and Latin iactare, with stream, the native Old English word for flowing water. Meteorologists coined the compound in the 1940s for the upper wind maximum.
intro.cn: jet stream 由 jet 与 stream 组合。jet 经古法语 jeter「投掷」来自拉丁 iactare；stream 是古英语本族词，指流动的水。气象学家在 20 世纪 40 年代用这个复合词指上层风的最大值。

items.en: Latin iactare 'to throw, to hurl' is the frequentative of iacere; through Old French jeter it gave English jet, a fast stream of something thrown out.
items.cn: 拉丁 iactare「投、掷」是 iacere 的反复式；经古法语 jeter 给出英语 jet，指被喷出的高速流。

items.en: Stream is the native word for a flowing body of water, so the compound compares air to water.
items.cn: stream 是表示流动水体的本族词，因此复合词把空气比作水。

items.en: Pilots in the Second World War met unexpectedly strong upper winds; the phenomenon was named in the 1940s.
items.cn: 二战飞行员遭遇了意外的上层强风；这一现象在 20 世纪 40 年代获得名称。

items.en: Post-war meteorology explained the jet as a response to the temperature contrast between tropical and polar air.
items.cn: 战后气象学把急流解释为对热带与极地空气温差的响应。

items.en: Numerical models made the jet's waves central to medium-range forecasting and aviation routing.
items.cn: 数值模式使急流的波动成为中期预报与航空航线规划的核心。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact year and the first author of the term are reported differently; the elements and their meanings are themselves not in doubt.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：该术语的确切年份与首创者各家记述不同；其构成成分与含义本身并无疑义。

note.en: Group one holds phrases and terms that look or sound like the meteorological jet stream; group two holds other names for the upper-level flow.
note.cn: 第一组是字形或读音近似气象术语的词组；第二组是上层气流的其他名称。

entries.definition: A fast stream of gas or liquid, or an aircraft engine; the compound uses only the first of these.
entries.definitionCN: 气体或液体的高速流，或喷气发动机；复合词只用前者。

entries.definition: A warm ocean current in the Atlantic; it shares the water word but is not part of the atmosphere.
entries.definitionCN: 大西洋中的暖洋流；共享「水流」这一词，但不在大气中。

entries.definition: The fatigue caused by crossing time zones quickly; it borrows jet from air travel, not from the wind.
entries.definitionCN: 快速跨越时区造成的疲劳；其 jet 借自航空旅行，而非风。

entries.definition: The broad mid-latitude westerly flow within which the jet stream is embedded; wider and slower.
entries.definitionCN: 急流所嵌入的中纬度宽广西风气流；更宽也更慢。

entries.definition: Any wind flow in the upper troposphere; the jet stream is its narrow, fastest part.
entries.definitionCN: 对流层上部的任何气流；急流是其中最窄最快的部分。

entries.definition: The vertical shear of the horizontal wind produced by temperature gradients; the jet is explained through it.
entries.definitionCN: 由温度梯度产生的水平风垂直切变；急流借它得到解释。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin source of jet, the real water word and the real meteorological purpose.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：喷流一词真实的拉丁来源、真实的「水流」词，以及真实的气象用途。

normal.en: Jet is a fast stream thrown out; stream is flowing water: air behaves like both.
normal.cn: jet 是喷出的高速流，stream 是流动的水：空气兼具两者特征。

normal.en: Two jets: polar and subtropical.
normal.cn: 两条急流：极地急流与副热带急流。

normal.en: It steers surface lows, so it works as a rail.
normal.cn: 它引导地面低压，因此像一条轨道。

normal.en: Flying east with it saves time; flying west against it costs time.
normal.cn: 顺它向东省时，逆它向西费时。

normal.en: Near the jet, wind shear causes clear-air turbulence without cloud.
normal.cn: 急流附近的风切变会在无云时造成晴空颠簸。

abstract.en: Picture a river of air drawn thin and fast, with weather hanging from it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条被拉得又细又快的空气之河，天气挂在它下面。

abstract.en: Picture an aircraft that gains speed without burning more fuel.
abstract.cn: 想象一架不烧更多油却变快的飞机。

abstract.en: Picture a channel so fast that nothing inside it can slow down.
abstract.cn: 想象一条快到其中任何东西都无法减速的通道。

examples.en: The jet stream split, sending cold air south and warm air north.
examples.cn: 急流分成两支，把冷空气送向南、暖空气送向北。

examples.en: Forecasters watch the jet stream to place the rain band.
examples.cn: 预报员观察急流以确定雨带位置。

examples.en: The return flight took longer because it flew against the jet stream.
examples.cn: 返程航班因逆着急流飞行而耗时更久。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「jet（喷射）+ stream（水流）」——像喷射水流一样的高空急流 → 急流

root: jet 经古法语 jeter「投掷」出自拉丁 iactare（iacere 的反复式）；stream 为古英语本族词，指流动的水。复合词由气象学在 20 世纪 40 年代造出，指上层风的最大值。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the upper wind band itself to its polar and subtropical forms, its effects on flight, on storms, on turbulence, its seasonal drift and finally its use as an image of any fast channel.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从上层风带本身，走到极地与副热带两种形态、对飞行的影响、对风暴的引导、对颠簸的作用、季节性漂移，最后用作任何快速通道的意象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river of air pulled thin and fast, with everything below hanging from it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被拉得又细又快的空气之河，下方一切都挂在它上面。

branches.en: ONE PHENOMENON, THREE NAMES: the general band and its polar and subtropical forms.
branches.cn: 同一现象三种名称：一般风带及其极地、副热带两种形态。

branches.en: FLIGHT: flying with the flow adds speed; flying against it subtracts.
branches.cn: 飞行：顺流加速，逆流减速。

branches.en: STEERING: surface lows follow the rails above them.
branches.cn: 引导：地面低压沿着上方的轨道走。

branches.en: SHEAR: fast air beside slow air becomes turbulent even in clear sky.
branches.cn: 切变：快空气贴着慢空气，即使晴空也会起湍流。

branches.en: DRIFT AND METAPHOR: the rail moves with the season, and any fast channel borrows its name.
branches.cn: 漂移与比喻：轨道随季节移动，任何快速通道都借用它的名字。

intro.en: Jet stream is a modern English compound of a French-derived noun and a native noun, so its parts are best read as two words rather than as affixes.
intro.cn: jet stream 是现代英语复合词，由一个法语来源名词与一个本族名词构成，因此宜按两个词来读，而非按词缀。

latinIntro.en: Only jet has a Latin ancestor, iactare; stream is Germanic, and no Latin prefix is involved.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 jet 有拉丁祖先 iactare；stream 属日耳曼语，且不涉及任何拉丁前缀。

items.structure: jet (noun from Old French jeter, Latin iactare)
items.example: A jet of water cut the soil.
The stream ran fast after the rain.

items.meaning: of a jet or of jets
items.example: Jet aircraft cross the ocean in hours.
items.exampleCN: 喷气飞机数小时就跨越海洋。

items.example: The polar jet sits farther north in summer.
items.exampleCN: 极地急流在夏季位置更北。

items.example: The subtropical jet is highest in winter.
items.exampleCN: 副热带急流在冬季最强。

items.meaning: a local maximum within the jet
items.example: A jet streak crossed the ridge.

items.meaning: a downbend in the upper flow
items.example: The jet stream trough deepened over the coast.
items.exampleCN: 急流槽在海岸上空加深。

items.meaning: the altitude of the jet core
items.example: Ice crystals persist at jet-stream level.
items.exampleCN: 冰晶在急流高度层持续存在。

latinEntries.meaning: to throw about, to hurl repeatedly

definition_zh: 顺便提一句；附带地；偶然地
definition_en: as a minor or secondary matter, or by chance rather than by design
core_image: 主线旁边的一条小岔路，走进去几步就能回来
scene: 会议记录写到末尾时补了一句与主题无关的小事。 Incidentally, the office will be closed on Friday afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里用作句首补充（第 2 个义项：句首旁白，转入次要信息）；句意为顺便提一下，办公室周五下午关门。

pos.zh: 顺便提一句；附带地；偶然地

senses.title: By the way
senses.definition: used to introduce a remark that is not central to the main topic
senses.definitionCN: 用来引入一句与主要话题无关的补充
senses.example: Incidentally, I met your sister at the market.
senses.exampleCN: 顺便说一句，我在市场上遇见了你妹妹。
senses.why: As a discourse marker it signals a change of footing: the following words are an aside, not the point.
senses.whyCN: 作为话语标记，它标示立场转换：接下来的话是旁枝，而不是重点。

senses.title: Sentence-opening aside
senses.definition: placed at the start of a sentence to mark a digression
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，标明接下来是一段岔开的话
senses.example: Incidentally, the museum has extended its hours.
senses.exampleCN: 顺便提一下，博物馆延长了开放时间。
senses.why: The initial position is the clearest signal that the sentence is parenthetical to the larger discussion.
senses.whyCN: 句首位置是最清楚的信号，说明这句话对更大的讨论而言只是插入语。

senses.title: As a side effect
senses.definition: as a secondary result that was not the main purpose
senses.definitionCN: 作为并非主要目的的次要结果
senses.example: The new drainage scheme incidentally reduced mosquito numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 新的排水方案附带地减少了蚊虫数量。
senses.why: Here the word describes a real consequence that came along with another aim, not a conversational aside.
senses.whyCN: 这里描述的是伴随另一目标而来的真实后果，而不是对话中的插话。

senses.title: In passing
senses.definition: mentioned briefly without being made the focus
senses.definitionCN: 简短提及，却不把它当作重点
senses.example: The report incidentally notes a rise in applications.
senses.exampleCN: 报告顺带提到申请人数有所上升。
senses.why: The adverb lowers the information's prominence; the writer does not want it treated as a finding.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词降低了信息的重要性，作者不希望它被当作主要发现。

senses.title: By chance
senses.definition: as a result of chance rather than design
senses.definitionCN: 出于偶然而非有意安排
senses.example: The two researchers met incidentally at a conference.
senses.exampleCN: 两位研究者在一场会议上偶然相遇。
senses.why: This is the older literal sense: an event falls in with another without being planned.
senses.whyCN: 这是较早的字面义：一件事未经计划地与另一件事碰到一起。

senses.title: Parenthetical insertion
senses.definition: used between commas to insert a remark without breaking the sentence
senses.definitionCN: 放在逗号之间，插入一句话而不打断整句
senses.example: The building, incidentally, was designed by a local architect.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑顺便说一句，是由本地建筑师设计的。
senses.why: The commas reproduce the spoken lowered tone that keeps the remark outside the main assertion.
senses.whyCN: 逗号复现口语中压低语调的效果，把这句话留在主要断言之外。

senses.title: Secondary relevance
senses.definition: in formal writing, describing a connection that is real but not central
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文字中，描述真实但不居中的联系
senses.example: The clause is incidentally relevant to the question of liability.
senses.exampleCN: 这一条款与责任问题只是附带相关。
senses.why: Legal and academic prose use it to admit a link while ranking it below the main issue.
senses.whyCN: 法律与学术文字用它承认存在联系，同时把这一联系排在主要问题之下。

senses.title: Not the main cause
senses.definition: used of a factor that contributed without being the principal cause
senses.definitionCN: 用于起了作用但并非主因的因素
senses.example: Rising rents were incidentally worsened by the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 上涨的房租因新税而附带地变得更糟。
senses.why: The word separates accompanying factors from the main causal story, protecting the writer from overclaiming.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把伴随因素与主要因果链分开，避免作者把话说得过满。

intro.en: Incidentally comes from the Latin verb for falling upon, through its noun and medieval adjective, plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「落到……上」的动词，经名词与中世纪形容词，再加英语副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The verb cadere means to fall.
items.cn: 动词意为「落下」。

items.en: The prefix in-, meaning on or into, plus cadere gives incidere, to fall upon or happen.
items.cn: 表示「落到」的前缀与「落下」合成「落到……上、发生」。

items.en: The noun incidentia names an event that falls upon someone, hence an occurrence.
items.cn: 名词指落到某人身上的事，也就是事件、偶发之事。

items.en: Medieval Latin forms incidentalis, belonging to an incident, as a learned adjective.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语构成形容词，意为「属于偶发事件的」。

items.en: English incidental appears in the seventeenth century, and the adverb adds the usual suffix; the exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语形容词在十七世纪出现，副词再加常见后缀；确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: Modern English splits the adverb between chance events and conversational asides.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个副词分用于偶然事件与会话中的顺便补充。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin falling-root, including a word built with a together-prefix; the second group contrasts side remarks, chance events and true accidents.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「落下」词根，其中包括带「共同」前缀的词；第二组对照旁枝补充、偶然事件与真正的事故。

entries.definition: An event, often a minor or unpleasant one.
entries.definitionCN: 事件，常指较小或不愉快的事。

entries.definition: Happening as a minor accompaniment rather than as a main aim.
entries.definitionCN: 作为次要伴随而非主要目的发生的。

entries.definition: The rate at which something occurs.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生的比率；发生率。

entries.definition: Two events falling together by chance; built with a together-prefix on the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 两件事偶然同时发生；同一词根加「共同」前缀构成。

entries.definition: A conversational formula for adding a side remark.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中补充旁枝信息的固定说法。

entries.definition: Briefly, while dealing with something else.
entries.definitionCN: 在处理别的事情时顺带地。

entries.definition: Unintentionally, often with the idea of a mishap or error.
entries.definitionCN: 非有意地，常含失误或事故的意味。

entries.definition: As an inserted remark that interrupts the main line.
entries.definitionCN: 作为打断主线的插入说明。

entries.definition: As a remark directed away from the main subject.
entries.definitionCN: 作为偏离主题的一句旁白。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real falling-root and the real difference between an aside and mere chance.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「落下」词根，并区分「旁枝补充」与「纯属偶然」。

normal.en: The root means to fall upon, so an incidental remark simply drops in beside the main point.
normal.cn: 词根意为「落到……上」，所以附带的一句话只是落在主题旁边。

normal.en: Said first in a sentence, it holds up a small sign that reads this way for a moment.
normal.cn: 放在句首，它像举起一块小牌子：这里只是岔开一下。

normal.en: Between commas it is spoken in a lower voice, outside the main claim.
normal.cn: 夹在逗号之间时，它像压低嗓音说出，站在主要断言之外。

normal.en: A side effect is real but nobody planned it, which is the working sense in reports.
normal.cn: 附带结果真实存在却无人计划，这是报告里的常用义。

normal.en: By chance is the older sense: two paths cross without an appointment.
normal.cn: 「偶然」是较早的义项：两条路没有约好就交叉了。

abstract.en: An aside is a way of saying something while pretending not to insist on it.
abstract.cn: 旁白是一种说着某话、却假装并不坚持的说法。

abstract.en: The word lets a writer keep a fact without giving it a place in the argument.
abstract.cn: 这个词让作者保住一个事实，却不给它论证中的位置。

abstract.en: Chance here is not mystery but the absence of a plan.
abstract.cn: 这里的偶然不是神秘，而是没有计划。

examples.en: Incidentally, the train times changed again this week.
examples.cn: 顺便说一句，火车时刻这周又变了。

examples.en: The repair incidentally fixed a small leak in the roof.
examples.cn: 这次维修附带地修好了屋顶的一处小漏水。

examples.en: The two ideas were incidentally connected, not deliberately paired.
examples.cn: 这两个想法只是偶然相关，并非有意配对。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因此等特利」——因此顺带提一句，只是旁枝

root: 拉丁语动词「落到……上」引申为「发生」，其名词指偶发事件，中世纪拉丁语再构成形容词「属于偶发事件的」；英语借入形容词后加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate conversational asides, sentence-opening digression, real side effects, passing mention, pure chance, parenthetical punctuation, secondary relevance and non-principal causes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理口语旁枝、句首岔开、真实附带结果、顺带提及、纯属偶然、插入语标点、次要相关，以及非主因的关联。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow side path beside a main road, a few steps in and back.
core.cn: 核心意象：主路旁边一条窄岔路，走进去几步就能回来。

branches.en: THE ASIDE: the conversational side remark and its sentence-opening form.
branches.cn: 旁白：口语中的附带补充及其句首形式。

branches.en: THE SIDE EFFECT: a real consequence that came with another aim.
branches.cn: 附带结果：伴随另一目标而来的真实后果。

branches.en: THE LOWERED VOICE: information mentioned without emphasis.
branches.cn: 压低的声音：提及却不强调的信息。

branches.en: THE UNPLANNED CROSSING: two paths meeting by chance.
branches.cn: 未约的交叉：两条路偶然相遇。

branches.en: THE OUTSIDE POSITION: parenthetical insertion, secondary relevance and non-principal cause.
branches.cn: 局外位置：插入语、次要相关与非主因。

intro.en: Incidentally is a Latin in-prefix, a falling-root, a noun and adjective layer, plus an English adverb suffix; the same root also builds coincidence.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「在内、落到」前缀、「落下」词根、名词与形容词层，再加英语副词后缀构成；同一词根还构成「巧合」。

latinIntro.en: The root cadere is about falling; prefixed forms name what falls upon a person, whether an event or a chance meeting.
latinIntro.cn: 词根的核心是「落下」；加前缀后指落到某人身上的东西，可以是事件，也可以是偶遇。

items.example: The prefix shows something falling onto a person or situation.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀表示某物落到某人或某种情形上。

items.example: The verb supplies the image of an event dropping in.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供事件「落进来」的意象。

items.example: The compound verb turns falling into happening.
items.exampleCN: 合成动词把「落下」转成「发生」。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a noun of occurrence.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成表「发生之事」的名词。

items.example: The noun is the base of the medieval adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是中世纪形容词的基词。

items.example: The learned adjective passes into English as incidental.
items.exampleCN: 这个学术形容词进入英语后成为「附带的」。

items.example: A together-prefix on the same root gives coincidence.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根加「共同」前缀，得到「巧合」。

items.example: The suffix turns incidental into a discourse adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成话语副词。

items.example: The noun measures how often an event falls.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词衡量事件发生的频繁程度。

definition_zh: 极地的；磁极的；极性的；截然对立的；极冷的
definition_en: relating to a pole, especially the earth's polar regions, or to opposite extremes such as magnetic or electric poles
core_image: 一根磁针的两端分别指向相反方向，越靠近端点，方向越明确
scene: 极夜里的气象站外风声不断。 Researchers at the station record polar winds during the long winter night.
sceneCN: 这里 polar 指「南极或北极地区的」（第 1 个义项：属于地球两极地带的）；句意为研究人员在漫长冬夜里记录极地风。图中可辨识物件：气象站、风向标、极光、雪地。

senses.title: Of the earth's polar regions
senses.titleCN: 极地的：属于南北两极地带的
senses.definition: relating to the regions around the North or South Pole
senses.definitionCN: 与北极或南极周围地区有关的
senses.example: Polar ice reflects most of the sunlight that reaches it.
senses.exampleCN: 极地冰面把到达那里的大部分阳光反射出去。
senses.why: Polaris 'of the pole' names the axis end; the regions around that end are the polar regions.
senses.whyCN: polaris 意为「极的」，指轴的端点；围绕这个端点的地区就是极地。

senses.title: Of a magnetic pole
senses.titleCN: 磁极的：与磁体两端有关的
senses.definition: relating to either end of a magnet, where its magnetic force is strongest
senses.definitionCN: 与磁体两端、磁力最强处有关的
senses.example: The north polar end of the magnet attracted the iron clip.
senses.exampleCN: 磁体的北极一端吸住了铁夹。
senses.why: Every magnet concentrates force at two ends, so the adjective polar describes anything belonging to those ends.
senses.whyCN: 每块磁体都在两端集中磁力，因此 polar 形容属于这两端的事物。

senses.title: Having electric polarity
senses.definition: relating to the positive and negative terminals of an electric source
senses.definitionCN: 与电源正负两极有关的
senses.example: The polar terminals must not be reversed.
senses.exampleCN: 极性端子不可接反。
senses.why: Electricity repeats the two-end pattern of magnetism, so the ends of a cell or battery are also called poles and their property polar.
senses.whyCN: 电学重复了磁学的两端模式，因此电池两端也叫极，其性质也称 polar。

senses.title: Polar in chemistry
senses.titleCN: 极性的：分子正负电荷中心不重合的
senses.definition: describing a molecule in which positive and negative charge centres are separated
senses.definitionCN: 描述正负电荷中心分离的分子
senses.example: Water is a polar molecule, which is why it dissolves salt so well.
senses.exampleCN: 水是极性分子，因此能很好地溶解盐。
senses.why: A molecule with separated charge ends behaves like a tiny magnet, so chemistry borrowed the magnetic word.
senses.whyCN: 电荷两端分离的分子行为像一枚小磁体，化学因此借用了磁学的词。

senses.title: Polar coordinates
senses.titleCN: 极坐标的：用半径与角度定位的
senses.definition: describing a coordinate system that fixes a point by distance from a pole and angle from an axis
senses.definitionCN: 用离极点的距离与相对轴的角度定位的坐标系
senses.example: The radar plot uses polar coordinates rather than a square grid.
senses.exampleCN: 雷达图使用极坐标，而不是方格网。
senses.why: The centre of the grid is treated as a pole, and every point is measured outward from it, so the system is called polar.
senses.whyCN: 网格中心被当作极点，每一点都从那里向外量，因此这套坐标系叫极坐标。

senses.title: Directly opposite
senses.titleCN: 截然相反的：处于两个对立端的
senses.definition: completely opposite in character or position
senses.definitionCN: 性质或位置上完全对立的
senses.example: Their views on the issue are polar opposites.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在这个问题上的观点截然相反。
senses.why: Two poles sit at the ends of one axis and face away from each other, so 'polar' pictures extreme opposition.
senses.whyCN: 两极位于同一轴的两端、彼此背向，因此 polar 用来比喻极端的对立。

senses.title: Extremely cold
senses.titleCN: 极冷的：像极地一样寒冷的
senses.definition: extremely cold, as in the polar regions
senses.definitionCN: 像极地地区那样寒冷的
senses.example: A polar wind swept through the valley overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 一夜之间，一股极冷的风扫过山谷。
senses.why: The polar regions are the coldest zones on earth, so the adjective extends from place to temperature.
senses.whyCN: 极地是地球上最冷的区域，因此这个形容词从地点延伸到温度。

senses.title: Of the pole star
senses.titleCN: 极星的：与北极星有关的
senses.definition: relating to the pole star, the star near the northern axis of the sky
senses.definitionCN: 与靠近天球北轴的北极星有关的
senses.example: Sailors steered by the polar star before compasses were reliable.
senses.exampleCN: 在指南针尚不可靠之前，水手靠北极星辨向。
senses.why: The star sits almost on the axis, so it is the polar star, the star of the pole.
senses.whyCN: 这颗星几乎位于天轴上，因此是北极星，即「极之恒星」。

intro.en: Polar comes from Latin polaris 'of the pole', from polus 'pole, axis', which was borrowed from Greek polos 'pivot, axis'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: polar 来自拉丁 polaris「极的」，源于 polus「极、轴」，而 polus 借自希腊 polos「枢轴、轴」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Polos meant 'pivot, axis, the end of an axis', and also the vault of the sky turning on that axis. Its deeper origin is uncertain; connections to a 'turning' root are hypotheses.
items.cn: polos 意为「枢轴、轴、轴的端点」，也指绕轴转动的天穹。其更深来源不确定；与「转动」词根的联系属假说。

items.en: Latin borrowed polos as polus, 'pole, especially the pole of the heavens'.
items.cn: 拉丁把 polos 借作 polus，意为「极，尤指天极」。

items.en: Polus plus -alis 'relating to' gave polaris, 'of the pole'.
items.cn: polus 加 -alis「与……有关的」构成 polaris「极的」。

items.en: English polar appears in the seventeenth century, first in astronomy and geography for the axis ends of the sky and earth.
items.cn: 英语 polar 在 17 世纪出现，最初用于天文与地理，指天空与地球的轴端。

items.en: In the nineteenth century physics and chemistry extended polar to magnetism, electricity and the charge separation of molecules.
items.cn: 19 世纪物理学与化学把 polar 扩展到磁性、电性与分子的电荷分离。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates only): the figurative sense 'directly opposite' and the chemical sense have no precisely recorded first English use; the Latin root is not in doubt.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：比喻义「截然相反」与化学义在英语中的确切首见年代未见记录；拉丁词根则无争议。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike words that are not about poles; group two holds words about cold, ends and opposition.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近但并不表示「极」的词；第二组是关于寒冷、端点与对立的词。

entries.definition: A tall fast-growing tree; it sounds close to polar but has nothing to do with axes or cold.
entries.definitionCN: 一种高大速生的树；读音接近 polar，但与轴或寒冷无关。

entries.definition: From sol 'sun': relating to the sun, as in solar energy; the first consonant differs from polar.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 sol「太阳」：与太阳有关，如太阳能；首辅音与 polar 不同。

entries.definition: From stella 'star': relating to stars, not specifically to the pole star.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 stella「星」：与恒星有关，并非专指北极星。

entries.definition: The state of having two opposite poles; it is the abstract noun built on polar, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 具有两个对立极的状态；由 polar 构成的抽象名词，并非另一词根。

entries.definition: Relating to the Arctic, the northern polar region named after the bear constellation.
entries.definitionCN: 与北极地区有关，这一北方极区以熊座命名。

entries.definition: Formally cold, often used of climate or manner; polar adds the image of the ice caps.
entries.definitionCN: 正式地表示寒冷，常用于气候或态度；polar 另带冰盖意象。

entries.definition: Placed on the other side or completely different; polar stresses the two ends of one axis.
entries.definitionCN: 位于另一边或完全不同；polar 强调同一轴的两端。

entries.definition: Relating to magnetism; polar can describe the ends of a magnet, while magnetic describes the force itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与磁有关；polar 可形容磁体两端，magnetic 则形容磁力本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek pivot, real magnetism and real coordinate geometry, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊「枢轴」、真实的磁学与真实的坐标几何，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Polos 'axis' + -ar: belonging to one end of an axis.
normal.cn: polos「轴」+ -ar：属于轴的一端。

normal.en: A magnet has two polar ends; a molecule with separated charge is polar too.
normal.cn: 磁体有两个极性端；电荷分离的分子也是极性的。

normal.en: Polar coordinates locate a point by distance from a central pole and angle from an axis.
normal.cn: 极坐标用离中心极点的距离与相对轴的角度定位。

normal.en: Polar opposites sit at the two ends of one line of argument.
normal.cn: 截然相反的观点位于同一争论线的两端。

normal.en: The polar star stands almost over the earth's northern axis.
normal.cn: 北极星几乎位于地球北轴的正上方。

abstract.en: Picture two magnets repelling each other no matter how you turn them.
abstract.cn: 想象两块磁体无论怎么转都互相排斥。

abstract.en: Picture a single street with one end in bright sun and the other under ice.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街，一端阳光明亮，另一端埋在冰下。

abstract.en: Picture a debate with two microphones at opposite ends of a long table.
abstract.cn: 想象一场辩论，两只麦克风分处长桌两端。

examples.en: Polar bears depend on sea ice to hunt.
examples.cn: 北极熊依赖海冰捕猎。

examples.en: Water is polar, so it dissolves many salts.
examples.cn: 水是极性的，因此能溶解许多盐。

examples.en: The two policies are polar opposites.
examples.cn: 这两项政策截然相反。

dict_mnemonic.text: pole（极）+ ar（……的）→ 极的 → 极地的、磁极的、极性的

root: 拉丁 polaris「极的」= polus「极、轴」+ -alis；polus 借自希腊 polos「枢轴、轴」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all begin at one end of an axis: the frozen regions, the ends of a magnet and a battery, separated charges in a molecule, a coordinate centre, opposite extremes, extreme cold, and the star that marks the northern end.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从轴的一端开始：冰封地区、磁体与电池的两端、分子中分离的电荷、坐标中心、对立的两端、极端的寒冷，以及标出北端的那颗星。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle whose two ends point opposite ways, each end defined by the axis it belongs to.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根两端指向相反方向的针，每一端都由它所属的轴来定义。

branches.en: PLACE AND TEMPERATURE: the polar regions are cold, and the word passes from place to weather.
branches.cn: 地点与温度：极地寒冷，词义从地点转到天气。

branches.en: PHYSICAL ENDS: magnetism, electricity and molecular charge all repeat the two-end pattern.
branches.cn: 物理的两端：磁、电与分子电荷都重复两端模式。

branches.en: GEOMETRY: a polar grid treats its centre as the pole from which everything is measured.
branches.cn: 几何：极坐标网格把中心当作极点，一切从那里量起。

branches.en: OPPOSITION: two ends facing away become a picture of complete disagreement.
branches.cn: 对立：两端背向而居，成为完全分歧的图景。

branches.en: THE SKY: the pole star marks the northern end of the celestial axis.
branches.cn: 天空：北极星标出天球轴的北端。

intro.en: Polar is pole plus an adjective ending; the same Latin root builds polarity, polarize and the international scientific vocabulary.
intro.cn: polar 是 pole 加形容词后缀；同一拉丁词根还构成 polarity、polarize 以及国际科学词汇。

latinIntro.en: Greek polos 'pivot' became Latin polus 'pole'; polaris 'of the pole' adds -alis, and English polar, polarity and polarization continue the family.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 polos「枢轴」变成拉丁 polus「极」；polaris「极的」加 -alis，英语 polar、polarity 与 polarization 延续这个词族。

items.example: The root names the line a sphere turns on.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指球体转动所绕的线。
拉丁缩短了这个希腊词。

items.example: Polaris also names the pole star.
items.exampleCN: Polaris 也用作北极星的名称。

items.example: The polar regions are warming fast.
items.exampleCN: 极地地区正在快速变暖。

items.example: The battery's polarity is marked on the case.
items.exampleCN: 电池的极性标在外壳上。

items.example: Bipolar disorder involves extreme mood swings.
items.exampleCN: 双相障碍表现为剧烈的情绪波动。

latinEntries.structure: polaritas, polaritatis (f., third declension, Medieval Latin)

definition_zh: 对数的；按对数刻度的；与对数函数有关的
definition_en: relating to logarithms, or expressed on a scale whose equal steps represent equal ratios
core_image: 一根尺子上的刻度越往右越挤，每一格代表的倍数却一样大
scene: 图纸的横轴上，刻度越往右越密，每一格代表同样的倍数。 The plotted points fall on a logarithmic scale that compresses the largest values.
sceneCN: 这里 logarithmic 指「按对数刻度的，即等长的一段代表相同的倍数」（第 2 个义项：对数尺度）；句意为这些点落在一条把最大值压缩了的对数刻度上。图中可辨识物件：坐标纸、不均匀的刻度、数据点、直尺。

pos.zh: 对数的；按对数刻度的；对数式的

forms.label: 比较级（多音节，由前置程度词构成）

senses.title: Of or using logarithms
senses.definition: connected with logarithms or carried out by means of them
senses.definitionCN: 与对数有关，或借助对数来完成的
senses.example: The old calculation was done by a logarithmic method.
senses.exampleCN: 这项老式计算是用对数方法完成的。
senses.why: the adjective simply marks anything that belongs to or works through logarithms.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是标记任何属于对数、或经由对数运作的事物。

senses.title: On a logarithmic scale
senses.definition: arranged so that equal distances on the axis stand for equal ratios rather than equal amounts
senses.definitionCN: 安排成轴上等长的距离代表相同的比值，而非相同的数量
senses.example: The plotted points fall on a logarithmic scale that compresses the largest values.
senses.exampleCN: 这些点落在一条把最大值压缩了的对数刻度上。
senses.why: a log scale keeps the ratio visible while squeezing the range, which is why it can hold both tiny and huge values.
senses.whyCN: 对数刻度在压缩范围的同时保留了比值，因此能同时容纳极小与极大的值。

senses.title: Logarithmic in form
senses.definition: describing an equation or expression whose unknown appears inside a logarithm
senses.definitionCN: 描述未知数出现在对数内部的方程或表达式
senses.example: The logarithmic equation is solved by rewriting it in exponential form.
senses.exampleCN: 这个对数方程通过改写成指数形式来求解。
senses.why: the equation is named after the operation that encloses the unknown, not after the growth of its solution.
senses.whyCN: 这个方程以「把未知数包住的那个运算」命名，而不是以解的增长率命名。

senses.title: Logarithmic growth
senses.definition: growth that slows steadily, so each further increase requires a much larger input
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐放慢的增长，越往后每增加一点都需要大得多的投入
senses.example: Memory research showed logarithmic growth in recall as study time increased.
senses.exampleCN: 记忆研究显示，随着学习时间增加，回忆量呈对数增长。
senses.why: because the logarithm of a number rises slowly, a quantity that grows logarithmically looks like it is levelling off.
senses.whyCN: 因为一个数的对数上升缓慢，按对数增长的量看起来就像正在走平。

senses.title: The logarithmic decrement
senses.definition: the logarithm of the ratio between two successive amplitudes of a damped oscillation
senses.definitionCN: 阻尼振荡中相邻两次振幅之比的对数
senses.example: The logarithmic decrement measures how quickly the pendulum's swing dies away.
senses.exampleCN: 对数减量衡量摆的摆动衰减得多快。
senses.why: a damping ratio is naturally spoken of through its logarithm, so the measured quantity carries the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 阻尼比天然要用它的对数来说，因此这个测得的量带着这个形容词。

senses.title: Logarithmic differentiation
senses.definition: a calculus method that takes the logarithm of both sides before differentiating
senses.definitionCN: 先对两边取对数、再求导的微积分方法
senses.example: Logarithmic differentiation made the product of five factors manageable.
senses.exampleCN: 对数求导法让五个因子的乘积变得好处理。
senses.why: the method works because logarithms turn products into sums, so the adjective names the step that unlocks the derivative.
senses.whyCN: 这个方法之所以有效，是因为对数把积化成和，形容词命名的正是打开导数的那一步。

senses.title: The logarithmic spiral
senses.definition: a curve that grows outward by a constant factor with every turn
senses.definitionCN: 每转一圈就按固定倍数向外扩张的曲线
senses.example: The shell follows a logarithmic spiral, widening at a constant rate.
senses.exampleCN: 这只贝壳沿着对数螺旋生长，以恒定的比例变宽。
senses.why: the radius of this spiral is an exponential function of the angle, so its description inverts into a logarithm.
senses.whyCN: 这条螺旋的半径是角度的指数函数，因此用对数来描写它。

senses.title: Logarithmic graph paper
senses.definition: paper printed with logarithmic rulings so that ratios appear as equal distances
senses.definitionCN: 印有对数格线的纸，使比值表现为等长的距离
senses.example: The students plotted the data on logarithmic graph paper to see the straight line.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们把数据画在对数坐标纸上，好看出那条直线。
senses.why: the paper is the physical form of the scale: equal spacing stands for equal ratios.
senses.whyCN: 这种纸就是刻度的实物形态：等间距代表等比值。

senses.title: Logarithmic complexity
senses.definition: describing an algorithm whose work grows with the logarithm of the input size
senses.definitionCN: 描述工作量随输入规模的对数增长的算法
senses.example: A binary search has logarithmic complexity, so doubling the list adds only one step.
senses.exampleCN: 二分查找具有对数复杂度，列表翻倍只多一步。
senses.why: each step of a halving search removes half the input, so the step count tracks the logarithm of the size.
senses.whyCN: 折半查找每一步都去掉一半输入，因此步数跟着规模的对数走。

intro.en: Logarithmic is logarithm plus the Greek adjective suffix -ic, which reached English through Latin -icus. It appears with the spread of logarithmic tables in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: logarithmic 是 logarithm 加希腊形容词后缀 -ic 构成，后者经拉丁 -icus 进入英语。它随对数表在十七世纪的传播而出现。

items.en: The Greek suffix -ikos formed adjectives meaning 'of or belonging to'; it was borrowed into Latin as -icus.
items.cn: 希腊后缀 -ikos 构成意为「属于……的」形容词；它被借入拉丁语作 -icus。

items.en: Latin -icus passed through French into English as -ic, the ending seen in arithmetic, geometric and logarithmic.
items.cn: 拉丁 -icus 经法语进入英语作 -ic，arithmetic、geometric 与 logarithmic 用的都是这个结尾。

items.en: Napier's logarithm was Latinized as logarithmus, and European scholars quickly formed adjectives from it.
items.cn: 纳皮尔的对数被拉丁化为 logarithmus，欧洲学者很快由它造出形容词。

items.en: English logarithmic appears in the seventeenth century alongside the tables and the new methods of calculation.
items.cn: 英语 logarithmic 在十七世纪与对数表及新的计算方法一同出现。

items.en: In later centuries the adjective attached to scales, spirals, decrements and algorithms, all cases where a ratio is read as a distance.
items.cn: 在后来的几个世纪里，这个形容词附着到刻度、螺旋、减量与算法上，都是把比值读成距离的场合。

items.en: The first English citation for the adjective is approximate; the suffix history and the base coinage are documented.
items.cn: 这个形容词在英语中的最早书证为约数；后缀的历史与基词的造词过程则有文献可查。

note.en: The first group shares the logarithm stem or the -ic ending and is easily confused; the second group names related scales and shapes.
note.cn: 第一组共享 logarithm 词干或 -ic 词尾，容易混淆；第二组是相关的刻度与形状。

entries.definition: The number itself; the adjective describes anything built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 指那个数本身；形容词则描述建立在它之上的事物。

entries.definition: The adverb, describing how something grows or is plotted rather than what it is.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，描述某物如何增长或如何作图，而非它是什么。

entries.definition: From logistikos 'skilled in calculation', but it names logistics and an S-shaped growth curve, not logarithms.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 logistikos「精于计算」，但指后勤学与一条先慢后快再趋缓的增长曲线，不是对数。

entries.definition: From logos in its 'reason' sense; it shares the Greek word but not the mathematical ratio sense used in logarithm.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 logos 的「理性」义；共享那个希腊词，但不共享 logarithm 所用的数学「比」义。

entries.definition: From the name al-Khwarizmi, not from logos or arithmos; it describes procedures, not scales.
entries.definitionCN: 来自花拉子米的名字，并非出自 logos 或 arithmos；描述的是过程，不是刻度。

entries.definition: Describes growth by a fixed factor; a logarithmic scale is the way that growth looks when flattened for viewing.
entries.definitionCN: 描述按固定倍数增长；对数刻度则是这种增长被压平后呈现的样子。

entries.definition: On a linear scale equal distances stand for equal amounts, the opposite of what a logarithmic scale does.
entries.definitionCN: 在线性刻度上等距离代表相等的量，与对数刻度的做法相反。

entries.definition: Squeezed into a smaller span; a logarithmic scale compresses a wide range, but the word itself says nothing about ratios.
entries.definitionCN: 被压进更小的跨度；对数刻度会压缩很宽的范围，但这个词本身不涉及比值。

entries.definition: Marked off in regular divisions; a scale can be graduated without being logarithmic.
entries.definitionCN: 按规则分度标出；一个刻度可以有分度却不是对数的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Logarithm plus -ic: the adjective of the ratio-number.
normal.cn: logarithm 加 -ic：比数这个词的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs logarithm, logarithmic, logarithmically and antilogarithm.
normal.cn: 同族词有 logarithm、logarithmic、logarithmically 与 antilogarithm。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: logarithmic scale, logarithmic spiral, logarithmic differentiation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：对数刻度、对数螺旋、对数求导法。

normal.en: On a log scale the small values get room and the giants get squeezed.
normal.cn: 在对数刻度上，小数值分到空间，巨无霸被挤扁。

normal.en: The -ic ending is the same one heard in arithmetic, geometric and chaotic.
normal.cn: 这个 -ic 词尾与 arithmetic、geometric、chaotic 里听到的是同一个。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler whose marks crowd together as the numbers grow, yet each gap still means the same ratio.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子，数字越大刻度越挤，可每一格仍然代表同样的比值。

abstract.en: Picture a spiral shell that widens by the same fraction at every turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一只螺旋贝壳，每转一圈就按同样的比例变宽。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase that adds one step for every doubling of the climb.
abstract.cn: 想象一段楼梯，每把高度翻一倍，才加一级台阶。

examples.en: Earthquake strength is reported on a logarithmic scale.
examples.cn: 地震强度按对数刻度报告。

examples.en: The logarithmic spiral appears in shells, storms and galaxies.
examples.cn: 对数螺旋出现在贝壳、风暴与星系中。

examples.en: Binary search is logarithmic, so the list can double for one extra step.
examples.cn: 二分查找是对数级的，所以列表翻倍只多一步。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「逻各节奏」的尺子——按比例的节奏一格一格量 → 对数的、对数刻度的

root: 英语 logarithm（对数，希腊 logos「比」+ arithmos「数」）+ 希腊—拉丁形容词后缀 -ic（-ikos / -icus）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses apply one measuring idea: equal steps stand for equal ratios. The idea appears as a method, a scale, an equation, a slow curve, a damping measure, a calculus trick, a spiral, ruled paper and an algorithm.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项应用同一个测量想法：等长的步子代表相同的比值。这个想法分别表现为方法、刻度、方程、缓慢曲线、阻尼量、微积分技巧、螺旋、格纸与算法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler whose marks crowd together on the right while each gap still means the same ratio.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子，右边的刻度挤在一起，而每一格仍代表相同的比值。

branches.en: THE MEASURE AND THE SCALE: anything done by logarithms, and the axis where equal steps mean equal ratios.
branches.cn: 测量与刻度：任何借对数完成的事，以及等步长代表等比值的那条轴。

branches.en: EQUATION AROUND A LOG: the unknown is wrapped inside the logarithm.
branches.cn: 包着对数的方程：未知数被裹在对数里面。

branches.en: SLOW RISE: the curve keeps climbing but each new unit costs much more input.
branches.cn: 缓慢上升：曲线仍在爬，但每一点新进展都要大得多的投入。

branches.en: DAMPING AND DERIVATIVES: a decrement read through a logarithm, and a derivative unlocked by taking one.
branches.cn: 阻尼与导数：用对数读出的减量，以及先取对数才打开的导数。

branches.en: SHAPES AND TOOLS: the spiral, the ruled paper and the halving search all turn ratios into visible distances or steps.
branches.cn: 形状与工具：螺旋、格纸与折半查找，都把比值变成可见的距离或步数。

intro.en: Logarithmic is a coined noun with a Greek adjective ending; the ending is old, the base is early modern.
intro.cn: logarithmic 是一个人造名词加希腊形容词词尾；词尾古老，基词则是近代早期的产物。

latinIntro.en: The Greek elements are logos and arithmos; Latin supplied the adjective ending -icus and the modern coinage logarithmus.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊构件是 logos 与 arithmos；拉丁语提供了形容词词尾 -icus 与近代造词 logarithmus。

items.exampleCN: 它提供这个词里「比」的那一半。

items.example: It supplies the number half of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它提供这个词里「数」的那一半。

items.example: The noun names the measure itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名那个量本身。

items.example: The antilogarithm returns the original number.
items.exampleCN: 反对数还原出原来的数。

items.meaningCN: 表示归属的形容词后缀
items.example: It is the same ending as in arithmetic.
items.exampleCN: 它与 arithmetic 用的是同一个词尾。

items.example: The code takes the log of the value.

definition_zh: 变化多端的；多才多艺的；难以捉摸的
definition_en: changing shape or form easily, like the sea god who could become anything
core_image: 一个人在同一分钟里换掉外套、口音和职业
scene: 他在同一周里当木匠、写剧本、又去修船，像换了一个人。 He worked as a carpenter, wrote a play and repaired a boat in the same week, a protean talent that no single title could hold.
sceneCN: 这里 protean 指多才多艺、形态多变（第 2 个义项：多才多艺）；句意为他在同一周里当木匠、写剧本、又修船，这种多变才能没有一个头衔装得下。

pos.zh: 变化多端的；多才多艺的；难以捉摸的

senses.title: Shape-shifting
senses.definition: taking many physical forms, one after another
senses.definitionCN: 接连呈现许多种形体
senses.example: The creature was protean, now fish and now stone.
senses.exampleCN: 那东西形态多变，一会儿是鱼，一会儿是石头。
senses.why: This is the mythic sense: the body itself keeps changing.
senses.whyCN: 这是神话义：身体本身不断改变。

senses.title: Versatile talent
senses.definition: able to do many kinds of work well
senses.definitionCN: 能把许多种活干好
senses.example: No single title could hold his protean talent.
senses.exampleCN: 没有一个头衔装得下他那多变的才能。
senses.why: The word praises range rather than depth.
senses.whyCN: 这个词称赞广度，而不是深度。

senses.title: Changing personality
senses.definition: of a person whose manner changes with the room
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人的举止随房间而变
senses.example: She was protean in company and silent at home.
senses.exampleCN: 她在人群里多变，在家里沉默。
senses.why: The social sense can be a gift or a warning.
senses.whyCN: 这个社交义项可以是天赋，也可以是警告。

senses.title: Protean disease
senses.definition: of an illness that presents itself differently in different patients
senses.definitionCN: 在不同病人身上表现不同的疾病
senses.example: The disease is protean, and two cases rarely look alike.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病表现多变，两个病例很少长得一样。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the myth because diagnosis needs a word for variety.
senses.whyCN: 医学借来神话，因为诊断需要一个表示多样的词。

senses.title: Protean career
senses.definition: of a working life that keeps changing field and role
senses.definitionCN: 不断更换领域与角色的职业生涯
senses.example: The protean career replaced the single employer.
senses.exampleCN: 多变职业取代了单一雇主。
senses.why: Modern labour gave an old myth a new address.
senses.whyCN: 现代劳动给一个古老神话换了新地址。

senses.title: Protean idea
senses.definition: of a concept that shifts meaning each time it is used
senses.definitionCN: 每次使用都会改变含义的概念
senses.example: Justice is a protean word in the speeches.
senses.exampleCN: justice 在那些演说里是一个变化不定的词。
senses.why: Ideas can be shape-shifters too, and harder to catch.
senses.whyCN: 观念也会变形，而且更难抓住。

senses.title: Protean artist
senses.definition: of an artist who refuses to stay inside one style
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝停留在一种风格里的艺术家
senses.example: The protean artist changed manner every decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这位多变的艺术家每十年换一种手法。
senses.why: Critics use the word both as praise and as suspicion.
senses.whyCN: 批评家使用这个词时，既是称赞也是怀疑。

senses.title: Elusiveness
senses.definition: of anything that will not hold still long enough to be defined
senses.definitionCN: 任何不肯静止到能被定义的事物
senses.example: The movement's aims were protean and its members disagreed.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动的目标难以捉摸，成员彼此意见不一。
senses.why: Here the word stops praising and starts asking for a definition.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词不再称赞，开始要求一个定义。

intro.en: Protean is named after Proteus, the sea god who answered questions by turning into anything else.
intro.cn: protean 得名于海神普罗透斯，他靠变成别的东西来回避提问。

items.en: Proteus was an old sea god who knew the future and hated to be asked.
items.cn: 普罗透斯是一位知道未来却讨厌被追问的老海神。

items.en: In the Odyssey Menelaus holds him while he becomes a lion, a snake and a tree.
items.cn: 在《奥德赛》里，墨涅拉俄斯把他抓住，他先后变成狮子、蛇与树。

items.en: English coined protean for anything that could take many shapes.
items.cn: 英语造出 protean，指任何能呈现多种形态的东西。

items.en: Geology used protean for minerals that crystallise in several forms.
items.cn: 地质学用 protean 指能以多种形式结晶的矿物。

items.en: Today it describes talents, careers, diseases and words, all in the same spirit.
items.cn: 今天它形容才能、职业、疾病与词语，都带着同一种精神。

note.en: The look-alike group is the prote- family; the near-meaning group separates mutable, versatile, mercurial and chameleonic.
note.cn: 形近组是 prote- 词族；近义组把「可变的」「多面的」「反复无常的」与「善变的」分开。

entries.definition: the shape-changing sea god.
entries.definitionCN: 能变形的海神。

entries.definition: a chain of amino acids in living tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 活组织中的氨基酸链。

entries.definition: the full set of proteins in a cell.
entries.definitionCN: 一个细胞里全部蛋白质。

entries.definition: an enzyme that breaks down proteins.
entries.definitionCN: 分解蛋白质的酶。

entries.definition: liable to change.
entries.definitionCN: 易于变化的。

entries.definition: skilled in many areas.
entries.definitionCN: 在多个领域娴熟的。

entries.definition: quick to change mood.
entries.definitionCN: 情绪变化快的。

entries.definition: changing to suit the surroundings.
entries.definitionCN: 随环境改变以相适应的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a man changing coat, accent and trade inside one minute.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一个人在一分钟里换掉外套、口音与行当」的画面。

normal.en: Protean is named for Proteus, the sea god who turned into lion, snake and tree to escape a question.
normal.cn: protean 得名于海神普罗透斯，他为逃避提问变成狮子、蛇与树。

normal.en: Think of one person with three trades and no single business card.
normal.cn: 想象一个人干三行，却没有一张能用的名片。

normal.en: Pro-TE-an: the stress sits on te, and the word keeps moving.
normal.cn: pro-TE-an：重音落在 te，整个词一直在动。

normal.en: Say PROH-tee-uhn; the first syllable is calm, the rest is the change.
normal.cn: 读成 PROH-tee-uhn，第一音节平静，其余部分是变化。

normal.en: Pair it with talent: a protean talent cannot be filed under one heading.
normal.cn: 把它和 talent 配对：多变的才能无法归档在一个标题下。

abstract.en: Protean praise and protean suspicion use the same word, because range and unreliability look alike from outside.
abstract.cn: 多变的称赞与多变的怀疑用同一个词，因为广度与不可靠从外面看是一样的。

abstract.en: A protean thing is hard to define, and hard to hold responsible.
abstract.cn: 多变之物难以定义，也难以被追究责任。

abstract.en: The myth survives because every age has something that will not stay in one shape.
abstract.cn: 这个神话活了下来，因为每个时代都有不肯保持一种形状的东西。

examples.en: He showed a protean talent that no single title could hold.
examples.cn: 他显出多变的才能，没有一个头衔装得下。

examples.en: The disease is protean, and two cases rarely look alike.
examples.cn: 这种病表现多变，两个病例很少长得一样。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses are one shape-shifter in different bodies: a creature, a talent, a personality, a disease, a career, a word, an artist and a movement.

branches.en: The mythic body that keeps changing.
branches.cn: 不断改变的神话身体。

branches.cn: 拒绝单一风格的才能与艺术。
