branches.cn: 不断换领域的职业与词。

intro.en: The prote- family is roughly about first things and forms: protein and proteome come from the Greek for 'first', while protean comes from the god of many shapes.
intro.cn: prote- 词族大致关乎「最初之物」与形态：protein 与 proteome 来自希腊语的「第一」，而 protean 来自那位多形的神。

latinIntro.en: Greek Proteus supplies the shape-changing, and the adjective ending -an turns a god's name into a description anyone can use.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 Proteus 提供变形能力，形容词词尾 -an 把神名变成一个任何人都能用的描述。

definition_zh: v. 分派；分摊；按比例分配（责任、费用、名额等）
definition_en: To divide something into shares and give each party its part according to a rule or standard, used especially of costs, blame, seats and resources.
core_image: 把一整块按份切开，谁该拿多少就分多少
scene: 委员会按各校人数分摊这笔经费。 The committee will apportion the grant according to enrolment.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：apportion 指按某个标准把总量分给各方，宾语常是费用、责任或名额。

senses.title: Share out by a rule
senses.definition: to divide a total into parts and give each person or group the share that a standard says is theirs
senses.definitionCN: 把总量切成若干份，按某个标准把各方应得的那一份分给他们
senses.example: The treaty apportioned the fishing rights between the two states.
senses.exampleCN: 条约在两国之间分配了捕鱼权。
senses.why: The word is ap- plus portion, literally to hand out portions, so a rule for dividing is always implied.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 ap- 加 portion，字面就是「把一份份递出去」，因此总隐含着一条划分标准。

senses.title: Assign blame or duty
senses.definition: to decide how much of the fault or responsibility belongs to each party involved
senses.definitionCN: 判定参与的各方各应承担多少过错或责任
senses.example: The inquiry refused to apportion blame before the evidence was complete.
senses.exampleCN: 在证据齐备之前，调查委员会拒绝归派过错。
senses.why: Here nothing physical is cut: the same picture of dividing a whole is applied to fault, which is why the verb sounds formal and legal.
senses.whyCN: 这里切的不是实物：同一幅「分整块」的画面被用在过错上，所以这个动词听起来正式、带法律味。

intro.en: Apportion is ap-, to, plus portion, from Latin portio, a share, which is related to pars, a part. English took it from Old French apportioner.
intro.cn: apportion 是 ap-「向」加 portion，后者来自拉丁语 portio「一份」，与 pars「部分」同源。英语从古法语 apportioner 借入。

items.en: Latin pars meant a part or a share of a whole. It gives part, partial, particle, apart and parcel.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pars 意为整体的「一部分、一份」。它产生 part、partial、particle、apart 与 parcel。

items.en: Portio named a measured share, the portion handed to one person out of a common stock.
items.cn: portio 指量好的一份，即从公共总量中递给某个人的那一份。

items.en: Old French portion kept the sense of a share, especially of food served to one diner.
items.cn: 古法语 portion 保留「一份」之义，尤指端给一位用餐者的那份食物。

items.en: Adding a-, to, gave apportioner, to deal out shares, the verb English later borrowed.
items.cn: 加上 a-「向」得到 apportioner「把份额分出去」，这就是英语后来借入的动词。

items.en: English recorded apportion in the 1570s, used from the start for dividing costs, land and duties.
items.cn: 英语在 1570 年代记录到 apportion，一开始就用于分摊费用、划分土地与职责。

items.en: Today apportion is common in law and public finance, with apportionment naming the act of dividing seats or funds.
items.cn: 如今 apportion 常见于法律与公共财政，名词 apportionment 指分配席位或资金这一行为。

note.en: The look-alike group separates apportion from appoint, which means to name someone to a post; the near-meaning group lists other verbs of sharing out.
note.cn: 形近组把 apportion 与 appoint「任命」区分开；近义组列出其他表示「分出去」的动词。

entries.definition: One share of a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 整体中的一份。

entries.definition: The ratio of a part to the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 部分与整体之比。

entries.definition: To name someone to a job.
entries.definitionCN: 任命某人担任职位。

entries.definition: The act of sharing out.
entries.definitionCN: 分配这一行为。

entries.definition: To set aside for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为某用途拨出。

entries.definition: To give out as a share.
entries.definitionCN: 按份分发。

entries.definition: To spread among many recipients.
entries.definitionCN: 分发给众多接受者。

entries.definition: To mark out as belonging to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 指定归属某人。

normalIntro.en: Apportion is ap- plus portion: hand a portion to each person, so the whole gets shared out by a rule.
normalIntro.cn: apportion 就是 ap- 加 portion：给每人递上一份，整块就按规则分完了。

normal.en: The usual objects are blame, costs, seats and resources.
normal.cn: 常见宾语是 blame、costs、seats 与 resources。

normal.en: It is formal: in speech say share out or split.
normal.cn: 它偏正式：口语可说 share out 或 split。

normal.en: The noun is apportionment, not apportionation.
normal.cn: 名词是 apportionment，不是 apportionation。

normal.en: Do not confuse apportion with appoint, to give a job.
normal.cn: 别把 apportion 与 appoint「任命」混淆。

normal.en: The pattern is apportion something among or between parties.
normal.cn: 常见句式是 apportion something among 或 between parties。

abstract.en: Picture a pie cut into named slices.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被切成署名份额的饼。

abstract.en: Imagine a bill split by how much each person ate.
abstract.cn: 想象按各人吃了多少来分的账单。

abstract.en: Think of seats handed out by population.
abstract.cn: 想象按人口分发的席位。

examples.en: The costs were apportioned according to floor area.
examples.cn: 费用按建筑面积分摊。

examples.en: It is too early to apportion blame for the crash.
examples.cn: 现在还为时过早，不宜归派事故过错。

examples.en: The board is apportioning next year's budget.
examples.cn: 董事会正在分配明年的预算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：ap-「向」+ portion「一份」——朝每位递上一份，按比例分完，就是分摊 apportion。

root: 拉丁语 pars「部分」生出 portio「一份」，古法语作 portion；加前缀 a-「向」成 apportioner「把份额分出去」，英语作 apportion，字面即「分成一份份给出去」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one act of dividing: cutting a real total into shares, and cutting fault or duty into shares the same way.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种划分动作：把实际总量切成份额，以及用同样方式把过错或职责切成份额。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one whole cut into shares, each party getting what the rule says
core.cn: 核心意象：把一整块按份切开，谁该拿多少就分多少

branches.en: A grant split by school size.
branches.cn: 按学校规模分的经费。

branches.en: Fishing rights divided by treaty.
branches.cn: 由条约划分的捕鱼权。

branches.en: Fault split between two drivers.
branches.cn: 两名司机之间划分的过错。

branches.en: An inquiry that waits for evidence.
branches.cn: 等证据齐备才下结论的调查。

branches.en: Both hand out portions by a rule.
branches.cn: 两者都按规则把份额递出去。

intro.en: Apportion is ap- plus portion, and the part root port-/part- also builds proportion, partial, parcel and apart.
intro.cn: apportion 是 ap- 加 portion，「部分」词根 port-/part- 还构成 proportion、partial、parcel 与 apart。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is pars, a part, and portio, a measured share; the prefix ap- is ad- assimilated before p.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 pars「部分」与 portio「量好的一份」；前缀 ap- 是 ad- 在 p 前的同化形式。

latinEntries.exampleCN: pars 产生 part 与 partial。

definition_zh: 合适的；恰好的；及时的
definition_en: arriving at a moment or in a way that suits what is being done
core_image: 手刚敲门，门就在那一瞬间打开
scene: 他辞职的消息正好在选举前一天传出，时机再合适不过。 News of his resignation came out the day before the election, an opportune moment by any measure.
sceneCN: 这里 opportune 指时机恰好（第 1 个义项：时机正好）；句意为辞职消息正好在选举前一天传出，时机再合适不过。

senses.title: Well-timed
senses.definition: happening at the moment that suits it best
senses.definitionCN: 发生在最适合它的那一刻
senses.example: The rain stopped at an opportune moment for the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 雨在仪式开始前恰好停了。
senses.why: The core is a match between event and moment, with nothing forced.
senses.whyCN: 核心是事件与时刻的吻合，毫无勉强。

senses.title: Convenient
senses.definition: placed or offered where it saves trouble
senses.definitionCN: 放在或提供在能省事的地方
senses.example: A bench appeared at an opportune spot on the long path.
senses.exampleCN: 长路上恰好在合适的位置出现一条长凳。
senses.why: The word can describe things, not only times; convenience is a kind of fit.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能形容事物，不只是时间；方便是一种吻合。

senses.title: Favourable
senses.definition: of a chance, offering an advantage if it is taken now
senses.definitionCN: 机会若当下抓住就带来好处
senses.example: The market was opportune for a small first sale.
senses.exampleCN: 市场对小规模的首笔销售很有利。
senses.why: Here the fit is between a condition and an aim.
senses.whyCN: 这里吻合的是条件与目标。

senses.title: Apt in speech
senses.definition: of a remark, said at the moment when it can be heard
senses.definitionCN: 话在能被听进去的时刻说出
senses.example: His opportune question saved the meeting an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 他那句问得正是时候，为会议省了一小时。
senses.why: Timing is the whole merit; the same sentence a day later would be an intrusion.
senses.whyCN: 全部优点就在时机；同一句话晚一天说就是打扰。

senses.title: Well placed
senses.definition: of a building or place, situated where it is most useful
senses.definitionCN: 建筑或地点位于最有用的位置
senses.example: The clinic stood at an opportune corner of the district.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所正好位于这一区适用的街角。
senses.why: Space repeats the logic of time: the right thing in the right place.
senses.whyCN: 空间重复了时间的逻辑：对的东西在对的地方。

senses.title: Politically timed
senses.definition: of a decision, made when the advantage outweighs the cost
senses.definitionCN: 在好处大于代价时做出的决定
senses.example: The tax cut was opportune rather than principled.
senses.exampleCN: 减税是出于时机，而不是出于原则。
senses.why: The word can be neutral or sly, depending on who is judging the timing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可中性也可带讥意，取决于谁在评判这个时机。

senses.title: Arranged at the right time
senses.definition: of a meeting or event, set for a time that suits everyone
senses.definitionCN: 会议或活动被定在适合所有人的时间
senses.example: The visit was opportune for both departments.
senses.exampleCN: 这次访问对两个部门都正合时宜。
senses.why: Planning can produce the luck that the word seems to describe.
senses.whyCN: 计划可以制造出这个词看似在描述的那种运气。

senses.title: Seemingly lucky
senses.definition: appearing to be a happy accident, whether or not it was arranged
senses.definitionCN: 看上去像幸运的巧合，无论是否被安排过
senses.example: It was opportune that the witness called that morning.
senses.exampleCN: 证人那天早上打来电话，实在凑巧。
senses.why: The word leaves open whether the fit was luck, skill or design.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不说明这种吻合是运气、技巧还是设计。

intro.en: Opportune began as a sailing word: a wind that blows toward the harbour is a wind that suits you.
intro.cn: opportune 起初是个航海词：吹向港口的风，才是顺着你的风。

items.en: Portus meant 'harbour', the place a ship is trying to reach.
items.cn: portus 意为「港口」，是船努力要抵达的地方。

items.en: Ob- meant 'towards, against', the direction a favouring wind must blow.
items.cn: ob- 意为「朝向、对着」，是顺风必须吹的方向。

items.en: Opportunus first described a wind blowing ships toward port, hence 'favourable'.
items.cn: opportunus 最初描述把船吹向港口的风，因此意为「有利的」。

items.en: English borrowed it through French, widening it from winds to hours and chances.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入此词，把它从风扩展到时辰与机会。

items.en: Today it mostly judges timing, and keeps a faint memory of the harbour in its calm, easy tone.
items.cn: 今天它主要评判时机，平静轻松的语气里还留着一点港口记忆。

note.en: The look-alike group is the opportun- family; the near-meaning group separates timing, convenience, advantage and aptness.
note.cn: 形近组是 opportun- 词族；近义组把「时机」「方便」「有利」与「贴切」分开。

entries.definition: at a suitable moment.
entries.definitionCN: 在合适的时刻。

entries.definition: suitability of timing.
entries.definitionCN: 时机的合适。

entries.definition: a chance to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的机会。

entries.definition: taking chances for advantage.
entries.definitionCN: 借机谋利的。

entries.definition: done at a useful time.
entries.definitionCN: 在有用的时候做的。

entries.definition: saving trouble or effort.
entries.definitionCN: 省事省力的。

entries.definition: giving an advantage.
entries.definitionCN: 带来好处的。

entries.definition: exactly suitable in the case.
entries.definitionCN: 恰好合适的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a door opening exactly as a hand knocks.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「手刚敲门，门就正好打开」的画面。

normal.en: Opportune hides port, the harbour: a wind blowing toward port is a wind that suits the ship.
normal.cn: opportune 里藏着 port（港口）：吹向港口的风，正是顺着船的风。

normal.en: Think of a door that opens at the instant of a knock.
normal.cn: 想象一扇在敲击瞬间打开的门。

normal.en: Op-por-tune: the middle sounds like 'port', the harbour where the timing is right.
normal.cn: op-por-tune：中间听起来像 port，时机合适的那个港口。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: uh-POR-tune, like a ship arriving.
normal.cn: 重读第二个音节：uh-POR-tune，像船入港。

normal.en: Pair it with moment: an opportune moment is one that costs you nothing to use.
normal.cn: 把它和 moment 配对：opportune moment 是一个用起来不费力的时刻。

abstract.en: Good timing is often the cheapest form of skill.
abstract.cn: 好时机往往是技巧中最便宜的一种。

abstract.en: The word asks not whether a thing is good, but whether it is good now.
abstract.cn: 这个词不问一件事好不好，只问它此刻好不好。

abstract.en: Opportune is not opportunistic: one describes a fit, the other a habit of hunting for one.
abstract.cn: opportune 不是 opportunistic：前者描述吻合，后者描述寻找吻合的习惯。

examples.en: News of his resignation came out at an opportune moment.
examples.cn: 他辞职的消息传出得正是时候。

examples.en: His opportune question saved the meeting an hour.
examples.cn: 他那句问得正是时候，为会议省了一小时。

examples.en: The clinic stood at an opportune corner of the district.
examples.cn: 诊所正好位于这一区适用的街角。

dict_mnemonic.text: op（朝向）+ port（港口）：风把船吹向港口，正是「及时、合适」的方向。

root: 拉丁语 opportunus（顺风的、合宜的），字面为「朝向港口」

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe a fit: a time to an event, a place to a use, a chance to an aim, a remark to a hearing, and a plan to a need.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述的都是吻合：时间与事件、地点与用途、机会与目标、话与听众、计划与需要。

core.en: A DOOR OPENING AS A HAND KNOCKS
core.cn: 手敲门的瞬间门正好打开

branches.en: A moment that suits an event and an event that suits a moment.
branches.cn: 适合事件的时刻与适合时刻的事件。

branches.en: A convenient thing and a well-placed building.
branches.cn: 方便之物与位置得当的建筑。

branches.en: An advantage to be taken and a decision timed for gain.
branches.cn: 可把握的好处与为利益择时的决定。

branches.en: A sentence said where it can be heard.
branches.cn: 在能被听进去之处说出的一句话。

branches.en: A fit that may be luck, skill or design.
branches.cn: 可能是运气、技巧或设计的吻合。

intro.en: The opportun- family grows from port: opportune is the favourable wind, opportunity is the harbour it brings you to.
intro.cn: opportun- 词族从 port 长出来：opportune 是顺风，opportunity 是它把你送到的港口。

latinIntro.en: Latin ob- gives direction and portus gives the goal; the adjective names a wind that serves both.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ob- 给方向，portus 给目标；那个形容词命名一阵同时满足两者的风。

items.example: The opportuneness of the visit was noted.
items.exampleCN: 这次访问的时机恰被注意到。
这个决定带着投机气味。

items.example: He importuned the clerk for an answer.
items.exampleCN: 他反复缠着职员要答复。

definition_zh: 预测性的；有预报作用的
definition_en: relating to or able to foretell something, especially in the phrase predictive of or predictive value
core_image: 一块试金石放在桌上，旁边摆着结果卡片：石头一碰，卡片就翻出未来的颜色
scene: 这里指「预测性的」。 The gene is predictive of heart disease but does not cause it.
sceneCN: 这里 predictive 是「能预示……的」（第 2 个义项：可用于预告某结果）；句意：这个基因能预示心脏病，但并不导致心脏病。图中可辨识物件：试金石、结果卡片、基因双螺旋图案。

pos.zh: 预测性的；有预报作用的

senses.title: Serving to foretell
senses.definition: having the function of saying what will happen before it happens
senses.definitionCN: 具有在事件发生前说明将会发生什么的功能
senses.example: The chapter is predictive rather than descriptive.
senses.exampleCN: 这一章是预测性的，而非描述性的。
senses.why: -ive marks a function. So predictive describes a tool, method or signal whose job is foretelling, not the foretelling itself.
senses.whyCN: -ive 标记功能。所以 predictive 描述承担预报任务的工具、方法或信号，而不是预报本身。

senses.title: Predictive of a result
senses.definition: used with of to say that one thing is a sign that another thing will follow
senses.definitionCN: 与 of 连用，表示一事物是另一事物将会出现的信号
senses.example: Low attendance is predictive of failure in the final exam.
senses.exampleCN: 出勤率低预示着期末考试不及格。
senses.why: The of construction makes the word a bridge: a visible sign here, an outcome there. The grammar itself carries the inference.
senses.whyCN: of 结构把词变成桥：此处可见的迹象，指向彼处的结果。推论由语法本身承担。

senses.title: Statistical model quality
senses.titleCN: 模型质量：预测得准不准
senses.definition: describing a model's capacity to estimate correctly values that are not yet observed
senses.definitionCN: 描述模型正确估计尚未观测值的能力
senses.example: The predictive accuracy of the model fell when the market changed.
senses.exampleCN: 市场变化后，模型的预测准确度下降了。
senses.why: Machine learning measures a model by future performance, so the adjective becomes a score: predictive accuracy, predictive power.
senses.whyCN: 机器学习以未来表现衡量模型，因此这个形容词变成一种分数：预测准确度、预测力。

senses.title: Predictive validity
senses.titleCN: 预测效度：测出来的分数管不管用
senses.definition: in testing, the extent to which a score forecasts later performance
senses.definitionCN: 在测验中，分数能预告后续表现的程度
senses.example: The admissions test has good predictive validity for first-year grades.
senses.exampleCN: 这项入学考试对一年级成绩有良好的预测效度。
senses.why: Psychometrics needed a term for a test that predicts rather than describes. Predictive validity names that specific evidence relation.
senses.whyCN: 心理测量学需要一个词指“预测而非描述”的测验。预测效度命名了这一特定的证据关系。

senses.title: Predictive text and coding
senses.titleCN: 输入法联想：猜你要打什么
senses.definition: describing software that suggests the next word or symbol from patterns already typed
senses.definitionCN: 描述根据已输入的模式提示下一个词或符号的软件功能
senses.example: Predictive text guessed the word before she finished typing.
senses.exampleCN: 她还没打完，联想输入就猜出了这个词。
senses.why: The software repeats the same act as a human forecaster, only faster: from what has come, infer what comes next.
senses.whyCN: 软件重复了人类预报者的动作，只是更快：从已出现的推断下一个。

senses.title: Predictive maintenance
senses.titleCN: 预测性维护：坏之前先修
senses.definition: describing inspection scheduled from sensor data that indicate coming failure
senses.definitionCN: 描述依据传感器数据显示的即将故障而安排的检修
senses.example: Predictive maintenance cut unplanned downtime by half.
senses.exampleCN: 预测性维护把非计划停机减少了一半。
senses.why: Industry applies the word to machines: a vibration reading predicts a broken bearing, so repair moves before the breakdown.
senses.whyCN: 工业界把词用到机器上：振动读数预示轴承将坏，于是维修被挪到故障之前。

senses.title: Predictive policing
senses.titleCN: 预测性警务：按概率布警力
senses.definition: describing the use of data analysis to forecast where crime is likely, a practice that raises ethical questions
senses.definitionCN: 描述用数据分析预报犯罪可能发生地点的做法，该做法引发伦理争议
senses.example: Predictive policing shifted patrols to three districts.
senses.exampleCN: 预测性警务把巡逻转向了三个区。
senses.why: The adjective extends from objects to people and places, and that extension is exactly where the ethical debate begins.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从物件扩展到人和地点，而伦理争论正始于这一扩展。

senses.title: Predictive processing
senses.titleCN: 预测加工：大脑先猜再修正
senses.definition: in cognitive science, describing the view that perception works by constantly predicting input and correcting errors
senses.definitionCN: 在认知科学中描述“知觉靠不断预测输入并修正误差”的观点
senses.example: Predictive processing treats perception as correction of a guess.
senses.exampleCN: 预测加工理论把知觉视为对猜测的修正。
senses.why: The theory takes the word literally: the brain speaks before the world answers, then revises.
senses.whyCN: 该理论字面地使用这个词：大脑先于世界作答，然后再修正。

intro.en: Predictive is predict plus -ive, from Latin praedicere 'to say beforehand' (prae- 'before' + dicere 'say'). The suffix -ive comes from Latin -ivus and marks a capacity or function.
intro.cn: predictive 是 predict 加 -ive，源自拉丁 praedicere“预先说出”（prae-“在前”+ dicere“说”）。后缀 -ive 来自拉丁 -ivus，标记能力或功能。

items.en: dicere 'to say' is the base. It also gives diction, verdict and contradict, and is distinct from dicare 'to dedicate'.
items.cn: dicere“说”是基础词根，还产出 diction、verdict、contradict，与 dicare“奉献”不同。

items.en: prae- 'before' plus dicere gives praedicere, 'to say in advance'. The prefix fixes the forward time direction.
items.cn: prae-“在前”加 dicere 得 praedicere“预先说出”。前缀固定了朝前的时间方向。

items.en: English forms the verb predict in the 16th century from the Latin participle stem praedict-.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪以拉丁分词词干 praedict- 构成动词 predict。

items.en: -ive, from Latin -ivus, marks what a thing can do. Predictive therefore means 'having the power to foretell', not 'the foretelling itself'.
items.cn: -ive 来自拉丁 -ivus，标记事物能做什么。因此 predictive 意为“具备预报能力”，而非“预报本身”。

items.en: Statistics, psychometrics and computing turn the adjective into a measure: predictive power, predictive validity, predictive accuracy.
items.cn: 统计学、心理测量学与计算把该形容词变成一种度量：预测力、预测效度、预测准确度。

items.en: Predictive text, predictive maintenance and predictive policing extend the word from forecasts of nature to forecasts of behaviour.
items.cn: 联想输入、预测性维护与预测性警务把该词从对自然的预报扩展到对行为的预报。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dict- stem or the -ive ending; the near-meaning group also looks forward but differs in whether a forecast is made.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dict- 词干或 -ive 结尾；近义组也朝前看，差别在是否作出预报。

entries.definition: the forecast itself. The noun is the thing said; the adjective is the capacity to say it.
entries.definitionCN: 预测本身。名词是被说出的东西，形容词是说出的能力。

entries.definition: the part of a sentence that says something about the subject. It comes from praedicare 'to proclaim', a different branch of the same dicere.
entries.definitionCN: 谓语。来自 praedicare“宣告”，是同一 dicere 的另一条分支。

entries.definition: relating to reasoning from general rules to particular cases. It ends in -ive but comes from ducere 'to lead', not dicere.
entries.definitionCN: 演绎的。虽以 -ive 结尾，但来自 ducere“引导”，不是 dicere。

entries.definition: accurately foretelling what will happen, often with a tone of inspiration. It stresses revelation rather than method.
entries.definitionCN: 预言式的；有预见的。强调启示色彩，而非方法。

entries.definition: done in expectation of something, before it happens. It describes preparation, not a forecast.
entries.definitionCN: 预先的；提前行动的。它描述准备，不是预报。

entries.definition: relating to the likely course of a disease. It is predictive in a specifically medical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 预后的；关于病程的。是医学意义上的预测。

entries.definition: used to identify a condition already present. It looks at now, while predictive looks at next.
entries.definitionCN: 诊断的。它判断当前已有的状况，而 predictive 看下一步。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: -ive means 'having the function of', so predictive means 'functioning as a forecast'.
normal.cn: -ive 意为“具有……功能”，所以 predictive 意为“起预报作用”。

normal.en: The fixed phrase predictive of shows the grammar doing the work: a sign now, a result later.
normal.cn: 固定搭配 predictive of 让语法承担工作：现在有迹象，以后有结果。

normal.en: Predictive validity is a test score that predicts grades, not one that describes them.
normal.cn: 预测效度指能预告成绩的分数，而不是描述成绩的分数。

normal.en: Predictive maintenance repairs before the breakdown, which is the industrial version of the same idea.
normal.cn: 预测性维护在故障前修理，是同一想法的工业版本。

normal.en: The contrast pair is diagnostic versus predictive: know now versus know next.
normal.cn: 对照词对是诊断与预测：知道现在与知道下一步。

abstract.en: Picture a smoke alarm: it does not report a fire, it reports the fire that is coming.
abstract.cn: 想象一个烟雾报警器：它不报告火灾，它报告正在到来的火灾。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow before a person: the shadow arrives first and tells you who is next.
abstract.cn: 想象人之前的影子：影子先到，告诉你谁要来。

abstract.en: Picture a weather glass whose falling column speaks before the storm.
abstract.cn: 想象一支气压表，水银柱下降先于风暴开口。

examples.en: The survey has predictive power for later earnings.
examples.cn: 这项调查对后来的收入有预测力。

examples.en: High cortisol is predictive of burnout in this sample.
examples.cn: 在这个样本中，皮质醇偏高预示着职业倦怠。

examples.en: We need a predictive model, not another description of the past.
examples.cn: 我们需要一个预测模型，而不是又一份对过去的描述。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑瑞滴克替吾”音近 predictive：先扑上去、锐利地滴出答案，替你预告——有预测作用 → predictive 预测性的

root: 拉丁 prae-“在前”+ dicere“说”→ praedicere“预先说出”；praedict- 词干 + -ive（拉丁 -ivus，表功能）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe something that works as a signpost, pointing from present data to a later result.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述“充当路标”的东西，从现在的数据指向后来的结果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a touchstone that reveals what is coming.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块能显出后事的试金石。

branches.en: SIGN AND FUNCTION: the general function and the 'predictive of' link are the adjective's two grammar shapes.
branches.cn: 标志与功能：一般功能与“预示”搭配是这个形容词的两种语法形态。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: model accuracy and test validity both turn foresight into a score.
branches.cn: 度量：模型准确度与测验效度都把预见变成分数。

branches.en: MACHINE AND MIND: predictive text guesses the next word, and predictive processing says the brain does the same.
branches.cn: 机器与心智：联想输入猜下一个词，预测加工说大脑也在做同样的事。

branches.en: INDUSTRY: maintenance moves before failure once a reading can foresee it.
branches.cn: 工业：一旦读数能预见故障，维护就提前到故障之前。

branches.en: SOCIAL RISK: policing by prediction extends the word to places and people, and to ethics.
branches.cn: 社会风险：以预测布警把词扩展到地点与人，也扩展到伦理。

intro.en: Predictive is predict + -ive. The prefix pre- marks time, the dic- stem marks saying, and -ive marks the capacity, giving a word for tools that foretell.
intro.cn: predictive 是 predict 加 -ive。前缀 pre- 标记时间，dic- 词干标记言说，-ive 标记能力，合起来指能预报的工具。

latinIntro.en: Latin dicere 'say' → praedicere 'foretell'. English keeps the stem dict- and adds -ive, from -ivus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 dicere“说”→ praedicere“预言”。英语保留 dict- 词干并加 -ive（来自 -ivus）。

items.exampleCN: 经济学家预测增长放缓。

items.example: The marker is predictive of relapse.

items.meaningCN: 以预测的方式（-ly 副词）
items.example: The term is used predictively, not descriptively.
items.exampleCN: 该词用于预测，而非描述。

items.meaning: one who predicts or a forecasting variable
items.example: Body mass is a strong predictor.
items.exampleCN: 体重是一个强的预测变量。

items.example: The system is unpredictable under stress.
items.exampleCN: 该系统在压力下不可预测。

items.meaningCN: 可预测性（-ity 抽象名词）
items.exampleCN: 可预测性有助于市场运转。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 预言性的（晚期拉丁构成）

definition_zh: 蒸发；使蒸发；消失；使浓缩
definition_en: to change from a liquid into vapor, or to cause a liquid to do so; also to disappear gradually
core_image: 太阳照在湿石板上，水膜先变薄，随后整片湿痕无声地退去
scene: 太阳升高后，草叶上的露水一点点变少。 By mid-morning the dew has begun to evaporate from the warm grass.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「液体受热后变成水汽而减少」（第 1 个义项：液体汽化）；句意为到了半上午，露水已在温暖的草地上开始蒸发。

senses.title: Turn from liquid to vapor
senses.definition: to change from a liquid into vapor, usually at the surface and below boiling point
senses.definitionCN: 液体在表面、低于沸点时变成水汽
senses.example: Rainwater evaporates from the roof soon after the shower passes.
senses.exampleCN: 阵雨过后，屋面上的雨水很快就蒸发。
senses.why: The verb profiles the change of state itself, not the resulting loss or the tool used.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词凸出状态变化本身，而不是由此造成的损失或所借助的工具。

senses.title: Dry up completely
senses.definition: of a liquid, to disappear entirely by evaporation
senses.definitionCN: （液体）因蒸发而完全消失
senses.example: The pool evaporates in summer, leaving cracked mud.
senses.exampleCN: 这水塘在夏天干涸，留下龟裂的泥。
senses.why: When the last liquid is gone, the verb shifts from the process to its end point.
senses.whyCN: 当最后的液体消失，词义就从过程转到终点。

senses.title: Remove moisture by heating
senses.definition: to drive water or another solvent off by heating
senses.definitionCN: 加热把水或溶剂蒸掉
senses.example: The laboratory evaporates the solution to recover the salt.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室把溶液蒸干以回收盐。
senses.why: The transitive use makes evaporation an action performed on a material by someone.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法把蒸发变成某人施加于材料的动作。

senses.title: Concentrate a solution
senses.definition: to make a solution more concentrated by removing part of its solvent
senses.definitionCN: 除去部分溶剂，使溶液变浓
senses.example: Slow heating evaporates the broth until it thickens.
senses.exampleCN: 缓慢加热让汤汁蒸发，直到变稠。
senses.why: The purpose shifts from removing water to keeping what remains, which is the culinary and chemical use.
senses.whyCN: 目的从「除去水」转到「留下其余成分」，这是烹饪与化学的用法。

senses.title: Vanish figuratively
senses.definition: to disappear gradually, especially money, hopes or support
senses.definitionCN: （钱、希望、支持）逐渐消失
senses.example: The grant evaporated after the second review.
senses.exampleCN: 第二次评审之后，这笔资助就化为乌有。
senses.why: An abstract quantity is imagined as a volatile liquid that leaves no residue.
senses.whyCN: 抽象之物被想象成一种挥发后不留残渣的液体。

senses.title: Fade in intensity
senses.definition: to become weaker or less intense, as if dissipating
senses.definitionCN: （情绪、紧张等）逐渐减弱
senses.example: The crowd's anger evaporated once the referee explained.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判一解释，人群的怒气就消散了。
senses.why: Intensity is treated as a quantity that can be lost to the air, like heat or moisture.
senses.whyCN: 强度被当作像热量或水分那样会散失到空气中的量。

senses.title: Be lost from soil or plants
senses.definition: of water, to be lost from soil, leaves or other surfaces into the atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: （水）从土壤、叶片等表面散失到大气
senses.example: Moisture evaporates quickly from bare, compacted soil.
senses.exampleCN: 裸露板结的土壤里，水分蒸发得很快。
senses.why: This is the passive side of the water cycle: the water is not acting, it is simply leaving.
senses.whyCN: 这是水循环的被动一面：水并没有主动做什么，只是离开了。

senses.title: Emit vapor (archaic)
senses.definition: of a substance, to give off vapor or steam
senses.definitionCN: （物质）散发出水汽或蒸汽
senses.example: Early chemistry texts say that heated salts evaporate a sharp vapor.
senses.exampleCN: 早期化学文献说，受热的盐会散出刺鼻的水汽。
senses.why: The old sense focuses on what comes out of the substance rather than on the substance changing state.
senses.whyCN: 旧义关注从物质里出来的东西，而不是物质本身的状态变化。

intro.en: The Latin and French stages are well documented, while the deeper origin of vapor and the exact date of the figurative sense are less certain.
intro.cn: 拉丁与法语阶段有较清楚的文献记录；vapor 的更深来源、以及比喻义的确切首见年代则不够确定。

items.en: Evaporare is built from e- 'out of' and vaporare 'to steam', itself from vapor 'steam, vapor'. The image is steam leaving a liquid.
items.cn: evaporare 由 e-「向外」与 vaporare「冒汽」构成，后者又来自 vapor「蒸汽、水汽」。意象是蒸汽离开液体。

items.en: The verb is attested in Late Latin technical writing. Its noun evaporatio supplies the action noun used in modern science.
items.cn: 该动词见于晚期拉丁语的技术文献。其名词 evaporatio 提供了现代科学使用的动作名词。

items.en: Middle French évaporer passed the verb to English. The earliest English examples concern moisture leaving a body or a liquid.
items.cn: 中古法语 évaporer 把该动词传入英语。最早的英语例子讲的是湿气离开物体或液体。

items.en: Chemistry gave the transitive use 'to drive off a solvent by heat', which remains the laboratory sense today.
items.cn: 化学带来了「加热驱除溶剂」的及物用法，这一直是今天的实验室义。

items.en: The figurative sense for hopes, funds or anger is relatively recent. It is generally treated as an extension of the physical image, but the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 用于希望、资金或怒气的比喻义出现较晚。一般认为它是物理意象的延伸，但确切首见年代存疑。

note.en: The first group looks and sounds like evaporate but comes from other roots; the second group describes the same change, its result, or its reverse.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上像 evaporate，但词源不同；第二组描述同一变化、其结果或相反过程。

entries.definition: to move people out of a place. It comes from Latin vacuus 'empty', so the image is emptying a space, not vaporizing a liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 疏散；撤离。来自拉丁语 vacuus「空的」，意象是把空间腾空，而不是液体汽化。

entries.definition: to judge value or quality, from Latin valere 'to be worth'. The similarity is only in the opening syllables.
entries.definitionCN: 评估；评价。来自拉丁语 valere「有价值」，相似只在前几个音节。

entries.definition: to show clearly, from Latin vincere 'to conquer'. It has nothing to do with vapor.
entries.definitionCN: 表明；显示。来自拉丁语 vincere「征服」，与水汽无关。

entries.definition: to turn into vapor by any means, including boiling; evaporate is the slower surface process.
entries.definitionCN: 汽化。以任何方式变成水汽，包括沸腾；evaporate 指较慢的表面过程。

entries.definition: to become completely dry, focusing on the end state rather than the mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 干涸；枯竭。强调最终状态，而不是机制。

entries.definition: the neutral word for going out of sight; the figurative use of evaporate adds the image of volatile loss.
entries.definitionCN: 消失。中性的「看不见了」；evaporate 的比喻义多出「挥发式损失」的意象。

entries.definition: to become weaker or less vivid, often of color, sound or feeling; it stresses diminishing intensity rather than loss of substance.
entries.definitionCN: 褪去；减弱。多指颜色、声音或情绪变淡，强调强度下降而不是物质消失。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means 'out' and the base means 'steam', so the verb is 'steam out'.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「向外」，基础词意为「蒸汽」，动词就是「向外冒汽」。

normal.en: The family runs evaporation, evaporative, evaporator and evaporated milk.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 evaporation、evaporative、evaporator 以及 evaporated milk（炼乳）。

normal.en: Laboratory collocations: evaporate the solvent, evaporate to dryness.
normal.cn: 实验室搭配：蒸去溶剂、蒸至干。

normal.en: The transitive form takes an object; the intransitive form takes from or into.
normal.cn: 及物形式带宾语；不及物形式常接 from 或 into。

normal.en: The figurative sense usually pairs with money, hope, support or anger.
normal.cn: 比喻义常与金钱、希望、支持或怒气搭配。

abstract.en: Picture a wet footprint on hot stone shrinking until only a pale shape is left.
abstract.cn: 想象炎热石板上一个湿脚印不断缩小，最后只剩浅色轮廓。

abstract.en: Picture a pot of soup simmering down while the kitchen window fogs up.
abstract.cn: 想象一锅汤慢慢收浓，厨房窗户同时蒙上水汽。

abstract.en: Picture a promise written in chalk and erased by rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一句用粉笔写下的承诺，被雨冲掉。

examples.en: The sun evaporates the last pools along the riverbed.
examples.cn: 太阳把河床上最后几处水洼蒸干。

examples.en: Heat evaporates the solvent, leaving a thin film of crystals.
examples.cn: 加热蒸去溶剂，留下一层薄薄的晶体。

examples.en: Public confidence evaporated after the third delay.
examples.cn: 第三次拖延之后，公众信心消散了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一娃泼水，越泼越少」——水在太阳下变少、消失 → 蒸发

root: 拉丁语 e-「向外」+ vaporare「冒汽」，源自 vapor「蒸汽、水汽」；经法语 évaporer 进入英语。vapor 更深来源不确定，比喻义首见年代存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the same change of state but vary the viewpoint: the process, its end point, the person doing it, the purpose, the abstract extension, the loss of intensity, the passive water cycle and the old emission reading.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次状态变化展开，只是视角不同：过程本身、终点、施动者、目的、抽象延伸、强度衰减、水循环中的被动失去，以及古老的「散发」读法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a film of moisture thinning under the sun until it is gone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层湿气在阳光下不断变薄，直到消失。

branches.en: PROCESS AND END: the change itself and the moment when no liquid remains.
branches.cn: 过程与终点：变化本身，以及液体不剩的时刻。

branches.en: TRANSITIVE PURPOSE: heating removes a solvent either to clean a material or to concentrate it.
branches.cn: 及物目的：加热除去溶剂，或为净化材料，或为浓缩。

branches.en: METAPHOR: money and anger behave like volatile liquids, one vanishing, one cooling.
branches.cn: 比喻：金钱与怒气都像挥发性液体，一个消失，一个降温。

branches.en: PASSIVE WATER CYCLE: water leaves soil and leaves without an agent.
branches.cn: 被动水循环：水从土壤和叶片离开，没有施动者。

branches.en: OLD EMISSION: the substance is seen as giving off vapor rather than changing into it.
branches.cn: 古老散发义：物质被看作放出水汽，而不是变成水汽。

intro.en: Evaporate is the verb in a Latin-derived family whose members divide the work of naming the process, the device and the result.
intro.cn: evaporate 是一个拉丁来源词族里的动词，族内成员分担命名过程、装置与结果。

latinIntro.en: Latin vapor and vaporare supply the base; e- marks movement out, and -ate marks the verb, while -ation and -or name the action and the device.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vapor 与 vaporare 提供基础；e- 标记向外，-ate 标记动词，而 -ation 与 -or 分别命名动作与装置。

items.example: The prefix sends the vapor outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把水汽送向外。

items.example: The base names what the liquid becomes.
items.exampleCN: 基础词命名液体变成之物。

items.meaning: having been evaporated; thickened by evaporation

A vaporous mist covered the fields.

definition_zh: n. 大树枝，粗枝
definition_en: a main branch of a tree, thick enough to bear weight; also a cut branch used for decoration
core_image: 雪把一根粗枝压弯，几乎碰到屋顶
scene: 雪把一根粗枝压弯，几乎碰到屋顶。 A heavy bough bent under the snow and almost touched the roof.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bough 指树的大枝；句意是雪把一根粗枝压弯，几乎碰到屋顶。

senses.title: A main branch of a tree
senses.definition: one of the large branches of a tree, thick enough to carry weight
senses.definitionCN: 树上粗壮、足以承重的大枝
senses.example: A bough of the oak hung over the path.
senses.exampleCN: 橡树的一根大枝横在小路上方。
senses.why: Bough is the old word for a branch large enough to bear a person.
senses.whyCN: bough 是古词，指粗到能承载一个人的树枝。

senses.title: A cut branch used for decoration
senses.definition: a branch cut for wreaths, garlands or festive decoration
senses.definitionCN: 为花环、彩带或节庆装饰而砍下的枝条
senses.example: They hung lanterns from a pine bough.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把灯笼挂在松枝上。
senses.why: Once cut, the same branch becomes an object rather than part of the tree.
senses.whyCN: 一经砍下，这根枝就从树的一部分变成了一件器物。

intro.en: Bough goes back to an old Germanic word for a shoulder as well as a branch.
intro.cn: bough 可追溯到日耳曼语古词，既指肩，也指大枝。

items.en: Bog means a bough or a shoulder.
items.cn: bog 意为大枝或肩部。

items.en: The root bugan means to bend.
items.cn: 词根 bugan 意为弯曲。

items.en: Bough names a large branch.
items.cn: bough 指大的树枝。

items.en: The gh stays although the sound is gone.
items.cn: 虽然读音已消失，gh 仍留在拼写中。

items.en: Poets use bough for a leafy branch.
items.cn: 诗人用 bough 指带叶的枝。

items.en: Bough is now largely literary.
items.cn: 现代 bough 多用于文学。

entries.definition: A part growing out from a trunk.
entries.definitionCN: 从树干长出的部分。

entries.definition: A large branch, or an arm or leg.
entries.definitionCN: 粗大的树枝；肢。

entries.definition: A main branch, or the upper limb.
entries.definitionCN: 主枝；手臂。

entries.definition: A very thin shoot at the end of a branch.
entries.definitionCN: 枝梢的细枝。

normalIntro.en: Bough sounds like bow but means the thick branch it could be cut from.
normalIntro.cn: bough 读音像 bow，却指可用来做弓的那种粗枝。

normal.en: The gh is silent, so it rhymes with cow.
normal.cn: gh 不发音，与 cow 押韵。

normal.en: It is the largest branch of a tree.
normal.cn: 它是树上最大的枝。

normal.en: Old English also used it for a shoulder.
normal.cn: 古英语也用它指肩膀。

normal.en: A bough is thick enough to bear weight.

abstract.en: The arm of an old tree.

abstract.en: A curve of wood holding up snow.
abstract.cn: 托住积雪的一道木弯。

abstract.en: A branch heavy enough to have a name of its own.
abstract.cn: 重到配得上专属名字的一根枝。

examples.cn: 一根粗枝在冰的重压下折断。

examples.en: Birds nested in the highest bough.
examples.cn: 鸟儿在最高的大枝上筑巢。

examples.en: She wove boughs of fir into the arch.
examples.cn: 她把冷杉枝编进拱门里。

branches.cn: 横在小路上方的橡树枝。

definition_zh: （枪炮的）后坐；弹回；退缩；反噬
definition_en: the backward movement of a fired gun, and any springing or shrinking back
core_image: 枪托撞在肩窝上，整个人被推得往后半步，瞄准线随之抬高
scene: 猎枪一响，肩窝被枪托顶得往后一顿，瞄准线也跟着偏了。 The recoil bruised his shoulder before he could fire again.
sceneCN: 这里 recoil 指后坐（第 1 个义项：枪炮击发时的向后反冲）；句意为猎枪一响，肩窝被枪托顶得往后一顿，他还没能再开一枪就先被撞伤了。

senses.title: The recoil of a rifle
senses.definition: the backward push of a firearm at the moment of firing
senses.definitionCN: 枪械击发瞬间向后的推力
senses.example: The recoil of the old rifle left a bruise for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 那支旧步枪的后坐留下了一块淤青，整整一周才消。
senses.why: This is the physical sense the word was born for.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词诞生时所指的物理义。

senses.title: To recoil like a spring
senses.definition: to spring back after being stretched, compressed or struck
senses.definitionCN: 在被拉伸、压缩或撞击之后弹回原位
senses.example: The rope recoiled and threw the hook back at him.
senses.exampleCN: 绳子弹了回来，把钩子甩回到他身上。
senses.why: The same backward motion, now in a machine rather than a gun.
senses.whyCN: 同样是向后的运动，只是发生在机械而不是枪上。

senses.title: To recoil from a sight
senses.definition: to shrink back in fear, disgust or shock
senses.definitionCN: 因恐惧、厌恶或震惊而向后缩
senses.example: She recoiled from the offered hand as if it were hot.
senses.exampleCN: 她像被烫到一样，从伸过来的那只手边退缩。
senses.why: Fear borrows the body's backward motion.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧借用了身体的向后运动。

senses.title: The blow recoiled upon him
senses.definition: of a consequence, to come back upon the person who caused it
senses.definitionCN: 指后果回落到造成它的人身上
senses.example: The insult recoiled upon the man who had spoken it.
senses.exampleCN: 那句侮辱反噬到了说出口的那个人身上。
senses.why: The image turns moral: the shot hits the one who fired.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象转向道德：那一枪打中了开枪的人。

intro.en: Recoil comes from Old French reculer, 'to move backwards', built on cul, the rear of the body.
intro.cn: recoil 来自古法语 reculer（向后退），构词基于 cul（身体的后部）。

items.en: Culus named the rump, the rear of the body.
items.cn: culus 指臀部，即身体的后部。

items.en: Reculer meant to back up, the way a horse backs up.
items.cn: reculer 意为后退，就像马向后退。

items.en: English applied the verb to the kick of a gun.
items.cn: 英语把这个动词用到枪的踢击上。

items.en: Recoil then named the force and the distance of that kick.
items.cn: recoil 随后指那股力和那一段距离。

items.en: Later it also described shrinking from a sight.
items.cn: 后来它也描述因所见而退缩。

note.en: The look-alike group is the rec- verbs; the near-meaning group separates rebound, flinch, wince and kickback.
note.cn: 形近组是 rec 开头的动词；近义组把「弹回」「畏缩」「龇牙皱眉」「反冲／回扣」分开。

entries.definition: to call back to mind.
entries.definitionCN: 回想起；召回。

entries.definition: to set down in writing or sound.
entries.definitionCN: 记录；录下。

entries.definition: to tell in detail.
entries.definitionCN: 详细讲述。

entries.definition: to earn back a cost.
entries.definitionCN: 收回成本。

entries.definition: to bounce back after impact.
entries.definitionCN: 受撞击后弹回。

entries.definition: to draw back from pain or fear.
entries.definitionCN: 因疼痛或恐惧而退缩。

entries.definition: to shrink at a small pain.
entries.definitionCN: 因轻微疼痛而皱眉缩身。

entries.definition: the backward thrust of a mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 机械的向后反冲。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a shoulder taking the stock like a door taking a slam.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「肩膀像门被撞上一样接下枪托」的画面。

normal.en: Recoil is re plus cul, the rear of the body: the gun moves rearward.
normal.cn: recoil 是 re 加 cul（身体后部）：枪向后走。

normal.en: Picture the shoulder taking the stock like a door taking a slam.
normal.cn: 想象肩膀像被门撞上那样接下枪托。

normal.en: Say rih-KOIL; it rhymes with the coil that springs back.
normal.cn: 读 rih-KOIL，与弹回的 coil 押韵。

normal.en: The same word covers guns, ropes and human flinching.
normal.cn: 同一个词覆盖枪、绳子和人的退缩。

normal.en: Ask what pushes back, and what that push costs the body.
normal.cn: 问是什么在反推，这份反推又要身体付出什么。

abstract.en: Recoil is the price a force pays to its own source.
abstract.cn: 后坐是一股力付给它自身来源的代价。

abstract.en: Every action leaves a backward shadow we must stand in.
abstract.cn: 每个动作都留下一个向后的影子，我们必须站在其中。

abstract.en: Morally, recoil means the shot finds the shooter.
abstract.cn: 在道德上，后坐意味着子弹找到了开枪的人。

examples.en: The recoil of the old rifle left a bruise for a week.
examples.cn: 那支旧步枪的后坐留下了一块淤青，整整一周才消。

examples.en: The rope recoiled and threw the hook back at him.
examples.cn: 绳子弹了回来，把钩子甩回到他身上。

examples.en: The insult recoiled upon the man who had spoken it.
examples.cn: 那句侮辱反噬到了说出口的那个人身上。

root: 古法语 reculer（后退）→ re- + 拉丁语 culus（身体后部）

sensesIntro.en: Four senses follow one backward motion: a gun's kick, a spring's return, a body's flinch, and blame returning to its author.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项沿着同一种向后的运动：枪的后坐、弹簧的弹回、身体的退缩，以及责备回到发出者身上。

core.en: THE SHOULDER PUSHED BACK
core.cn: 被推回去的肩

branches.en: The gun's own backward push.
branches.cn: 枪自身的向后推力。

branches.en: A spring or a rope returning to shape.
branches.cn: 弹簧或绳索恢复原状。

branches.en: The body's retreat from something unbearable.
branches.cn: 身体对难以忍受之物的退避。

branches.en: Blame coming back to the one who spoke.

definition_zh: 海洋生态系统（海洋生物群落与其物理环境相互作用构成的整体）
definition_en: the community of marine organisms together with the physical environment they interact with
core_image: 从水面透下的光、随流漂动的浮游生物、吃它们的鱼、再把养分还给水的细菌，连成一台不停运转的机器
scene: 研究员把海草床、鱼群与水流放在同一张图表上分析。 The marine ecosystem depends on tiny plankton at its base.
sceneCN: 这里 marine ecosystem 指「海洋生物群落与环境构成的整体系统」（第 1 个义项：作为功能整体）；句意为海洋生态系统依靠最底层的微小浮游生物支撑。

pos.zh: 海洋生态系统（可数，复数 marine ecosystems）

derivatives.zh: marinus（拉丁「海的」）→ 海洋的：与海有关的
eco-（希腊 oikos「住所」）+ system（希腊 systema「组合体」）→ 生态系统：生物群落与环境构成的整体
eco-（oikos「住所」）+ -logy（学科后缀）→ 生态学：研究生物与环境关系的学科
ecology + -ical（形容词后缀）→ 生态的：属于生态学或生态关系的
ecology + -ist（从业者后缀）→ 生态学家：研究生态关系的人

senses.title: The system as a whole
senses.titleCN: 作为整体的海洋生态系统
senses.definition: the living community and its physical setting taken as one functioning unit
senses.definitionCN: 把生物群落与物理环境当作一个运作单位
senses.example: The marine ecosystem depends on tiny plankton at its base.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋生态系统依靠最底层的微小浮游生物支撑。
senses.why: ecosystem already means a community plus its environment, and marine narrows it to the sea.
senses.whyCN: ecosystem 本义就是群落加环境，marine 把它收窄到海洋。

senses.title: The producer layer
senses.titleCN: 生产者层：浮游植物与海藻
senses.definition: the photosynthetic organisms that capture energy at the base
senses.definitionCN: 在底层捕获能量的光合生物
senses.example: Phytoplankton drive the marine ecosystem's energy supply.
senses.exampleCN: 浮游植物驱动海洋生态系统的能量供给。
senses.why: every ecosystem needs an entry point for energy, and in the sea that point is mostly single-celled photosynthesis.
senses.whyCN: 每个生态系统都需要能量入口，在海里这个入口主要是单细胞光合作用。

senses.title: The consumer food web
senses.definition: the network of animals that eat producers and one another
senses.definitionCN: 以生产者及其他动物为食的动物网络
senses.example: Overfishing reshapes the marine ecosystem's food web.
senses.exampleCN: 过度捕捞改变了海洋生态系统的食物网。
senses.why: energy captured by producers passes through a branching chain of eaters, which is what the word ecosystem treats as its wiring.
senses.whyCN: 生产者捕获的能量经过分叉的取食链传递，这正是生态系统一词当作线路的部分。

senses.title: Decomposers and nutrient cycling
senses.definition: the organisms and processes that return nutrients to the water
senses.definitionCN: 把养分送回水中的生物与过程
senses.example: Bacteria recycle nutrients throughout the marine ecosystem.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌在整个海洋生态系统中循环养分。
senses.why: a system must close its loops, and decomposition is the return path that keeps nutrients available.
senses.whyCN: 系统必须闭合回路，分解就是让养分持续可用的返回路径。

senses.title: The physical environment
senses.definition: light, temperature, salinity, pressure and currents as the setting of life
senses.definitionCN: 作为生命环境的光、温度、盐度、压力与水流
senses.example: Light limits the marine ecosystem in deep water.
senses.exampleCN: 在深水中，光限制着海洋生态系统。
senses.why: the non-living half of the definition is real: without the physical setting there is no system to speak of.
senses.whyCN: 定义中非生命的那一半是实指的：没有物理环境就谈不上系统。

senses.title: A named type by setting
senses.definition: a particular system such as a coastal, open-ocean, deep-sea or vent ecosystem
senses.definitionCN: 沿岸、开阔海、深海或喷口等具体类型的系统
senses.example: The vent marine ecosystem runs on chemistry, not sunlight.
senses.exampleCN: 喷口海洋生态系统靠化学而非阳光运转。
senses.why: the same definition applies at different scales, so the phrase multiplies into named types.
senses.whyCN: 同一定义适用于不同尺度，因此这个短语分化出多种命名类型。

senses.title: A unit of services and impact
senses.definition: the system valued for fisheries, carbon storage and waste processing
senses.definitionCN: 从渔业、碳储存与废物处理角度被估值的系统
senses.example: The marine ecosystem provides food for billions of people.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋生态系统为数十亿人提供食物。
senses.why: policy needs a countable unit, so the ecosystem becomes the thing that supplies services and absorbs damage.
senses.whyCN: 政策需要可计数的单位，于是生态系统成为提供服务、承受损害的对象。

senses.title: A model and monitoring unit
senses.definition: the system represented in equations and tracked by indicators
senses.definitionCN: 用方程表示、用指标追踪的系统
senses.example: The model simplifies the marine ecosystem into a few dozen groups.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型把海洋生态系统简化成几十个类群。
senses.why: to predict change, scientists must turn the whole into variables, so the word also names the modelled object.
senses.whyCN: 为了预测变化，科学家必须把整体化为变量，因此这个词也命名被建模的对象。

intro.en: Marine ecosystem joins a Latin adjective to a twentieth-century coinage. Marine comes from mare 'sea' through marinus. Ecosystem was coined in 1935 from Greek oikos 'household' plus systema 'organised whole'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: marine ecosystem 把拉丁形容词接在一个二十世纪新造词上。marine 经 marinus 来自 mare「海」。ecosystem 一九三五年以希腊 oikos「家宅」加 systema「有组织的整体」造出。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mare 'sea' produced marinus 'of the sea', the source of English marine and maritime.
items.cn: mare「海」产生 marinus「海的」，是英语 marine 与 maritime 的来源。

items.en: Oikos meant 'house, household' and supplied the eco- of ecology and ecosystem.
items.cn: oikos 意为「房屋、家宅」，提供 ecology 与 ecosystem 的 eco-。

items.en: Systema meant an organised whole made of parts, and gave English system.
items.cn: systema 意为由部分组成的有组织整体，给出英语 system。

items.en: The botanist Arthur Tansley coined ecosystem for the physical system formed by organisms and their environment.
items.cn: 植物学家坦斯利造出 ecosystem 一词，指生物与其环境构成的物理系统。

items.en: Mid-twentieth-century oceanography and fisheries science combined the two words into a standard term.
items.cn: 二十世纪中期的海洋学与渔业科学把两个词组合成标准术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the phrase's earliest technical use is not consistently dated, though each element is well documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：这个短语最早的技术使用各家年代不一，尽管每个成分记载清楚。

note.en: Group one holds the scientific terms most easily swapped for marine ecosystem; group two holds the ecological units that sit at different scales.
note.cn: 第一组是最容易与海洋生态系统互换的科学术语；第二组是不同尺度上的生态单位。

entries.definition: The science that studies marine ecosystems; it is a discipline, while the ecosystem is what the discipline examines.
entries.definitionCN: 研究海洋生态系统的学科；它是一门学问，而生态系统是被研究的对象。

entries.definition: A particular place where organisms live, such as a reef or a vent; it is a component of an ecosystem, not the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 生物生活的特定地点，如礁或喷口；它是生态系统的组成部分，而非整体。

entries.definition: All the organisms living together in a place; it excludes the physical environment that ecosystem includes.
entries.definitionCN: 同一地点共同生活的全部生物；不含生态系统所包括的物理环境。

entries.definition: A near-synonym stressing the open ocean as a body of water; marine is the broader technical modifier.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，强调开阔海洋这一水体；marine 是更宽的技术限定词。

entries.definition: The general unit of organisms plus environment; it may be forest, lake or city.
entries.definitionCN: 生物加环境的一般单位；可以是森林、湖泊或城市。

entries.definition: A large regional community defined by climate, such as tundra or rainforest; it is far larger than one marine ecosystem.
entries.definitionCN: 由气候定义的大型区域群落，如苔原或雨林；比单个海洋生态系统大得多。

entries.definition: The network of who eats whom; it is one part of an ecosystem's structure.
entries.definitionCN: 谁吃谁的网络；它是生态系统结构的一部分。

entries.definition: The living organisms of a region taken together; it excludes water, light and temperature.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地区的全部生物；不含水、光与温度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek and Latin roots and real ecological levels, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊与拉丁词根以及真实的生态层级，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: eco- is oikos, a household: an ecosystem is a household of living things plus its house.
normal.cn: eco- 即 oikos「家宅」：生态系统就是生物的家户加上它的房子。

normal.en: marine is mare, the sea: the phrase simply puts the household in the sea.
normal.cn: marine 即 mare「海」：这个短语只是把这个家户放进海里。

normal.en: Four parts to remember: producers, consumers, decomposers, physical setting.
normal.cn: 记四部分：生产者、消费者、分解者、物理环境。

normal.en: Energy enters as sunlight or chemicals and leaves as heat; matter goes round in loops.
normal.cn: 能量以阳光或化学物进入、以热离开；物质则在圈里循环。

normal.en: Policy phrases mark the unit: ecosystem health, ecosystem services, ecosystem management.
normal.cn: 政策短语标出这个单位：生态系统健康、生态系统服务、生态系统管理。

abstract.en: A marine ecosystem is a city whose citizens never agreed on a plan.
abstract.cn: 海洋生态系统是一座市民从未商定计划的城。

abstract.en: It is a ledger where sunlight is deposited and heat is withdrawn.
abstract.cn: 它是一本账，存入阳光，取出热量。

abstract.en: The sea keeps its economy invisible; we see only the bankruptcies.
abstract.cn: 海把自己的经济藏起来；我们只看见破产。

examples.en: Nutrient runoff can collapse a coastal marine ecosystem.
examples.cn: 养分径流可能使一个沿岸海洋生态系统崩溃。

examples.en: The marine ecosystem of the shelf supports most commercial fishing.
examples.cn: 大陆架的海洋生态系统支撑着大部分商业捕捞。

examples.en: Scientists model the marine ecosystem to predict fish stocks.
examples.cn: 科学家为预测鱼类资源而建立海洋生态系统模型。

dict_mnemonic.text: marine（海的）+ ecosystem（生态系统）＝海洋里的生物群落加环境；记四部分：生产者、消费者、分解者、物理环境。

root: marine（拉丁 mare「海」→ marinus）+ ecosystem（希腊 oikos「家宅」+ systema「整体」，一九三五年造词）；短语为二十世纪海洋科学所立。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one working system: the whole, its producers, its consumers, its decomposers, its physical setting, its named types, its services and its modelled form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个运作系统展开：整体、生产者、消费者、分解者、物理环境、命名类型、服务，以及被建模的形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sunlight entering water, plankton capturing it, fish eating plankton, bacteria returning the nutrients.
core.cn: 核心意象：阳光进入水中，浮游生物捕获它，鱼吃浮游生物，细菌把养分送回。

branches.en: WHOLE AND SETTING: the system, then the water, light and heat that frame it.
branches.cn: 整体与环境：先是系统，再是框住它的水、光与热。

branches.en: PRODUCERS: the entry point where energy becomes food.
branches.cn: 生产者：能量变成食物的入口。

branches.en: EATING AND RETURNING: the food web, then decomposition closing the loop.
branches.cn: 取食与归还：先是食物网，再是闭合回路的分解。

branches.en: TYPES AND MODELS: real named systems, then the same systems in equations.
branches.cn: 类型与模型：先是真实的命名系统，再是方程中的同一系统。

branches.en: SERVICES: the system counted as food, carbon store and waste processor.
branches.cn: 服务：把系统计为食物、碳库与废物处理者。

intro.en: Marine ecosystem is a two-word technical phrase: a Latin-derived adjective plus a Greek-derived noun, each with a productive family.
intro.cn: marine ecosystem 是两词技术短语：拉丁语源形容词加希腊语源名词，各自都有能产词族。

latinIntro.en: Mare supplies marine; oikos and systema are Greek and have no Latin cognates, though Latin borrowed Greek systema as systema.
latinIntro.cn: mare 提供 marine；oikos 与 systema 属希腊语，在拉丁语中无同族词，尽管拉丁语曾借入希腊 systema 作 systema。

senses.title: The drawing out of a response
senses.definition: the act of drawing out a response, answer or fact from someone
senses.definitionCN: （名词）从某人那里引出回答、答复或事实的行为
senses.example: The elicitation of a clear answer took three separate interviews.
senses.exampleCN: 引出一个明确的答复，花了三次单独的访谈。

senses.title: The technique of prompting
senses.definition: a teaching or research method that prompts people to produce language or knowledge themselves
senses.definitionCN: （名词）促使人们自己产出语言或知识的教学或研究方法

intro.en: Elicitation is the noun of elicit, from Latin elicere, which joins ex- meaning out to lacere meaning to entice; the picture is a lure that draws something out.
intro.cn: elicitation 是 elicit 的名词，来自拉丁语 elicere，它把 ex-（向外）与 lacere（引诱）结合；画面是一个把东西引出来的诱饵。

items.en: Adding ex- gives elicere, to draw out by a lure.

items.en: English took elicit in the 17C for drawing out a fact or a response.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪借用 elicit，指引出事实或回答。

items.en: The noun elicitation named the act of drawing out.

note.en: Elicitation and extraction both end in -tion and both mean pulling something out, but elicitation uses a prompt while extraction uses force.
note.cn: elicitation 与 extraction 都以 -tion 结尾，都表示把东西弄出来，但 elicitation 靠提示，extraction 靠用力。

dict_mnemonic.text: elicitation ＝ elicit（引出）＋ -ation（名词后缀，表行为／过程）＝「引出这件事」。动词 elicit ＝ e-（向外）＋ licit（来自拉丁 lacere「引诱」，注意不是 licere「允许」）＝用诱饵把东西引出来。关键辨析：elicit 与 illicit 读音几乎一样，但 illicit 是形容词「非法的」（il- 不 ＋ licit 合法），拼写差一个字母，考试常考。三个高频术语直接背：requirements elicitation 需求获取（软件工程）、knowledge elicitation 知识获取（专家系统）、elicitation technique 启发式提问（语言教学）。近义 extraction 靠用力拔（extract a tooth 拔牙），evocation 靠唤起记忆情感，prompting 靠给提示。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）＋ lacere（引诱）→ elicere（引出）→ elicit ＋ -ation → elicitation（引出；诱出）
